questions.passage:
By Rosanne Villalobos
THISTLETON (6 February)—Larchmere Print and Packaging will move its operations to a larger site north of town, the firm confirmed this week. Its Wesley Street premises can no longer hold the presses needed to meet rising orders for folded cartons. The new building at Hollowbrook Industrial Park offers 4,200 square meters, nearly twice the present production area.
"We have been turning work away for want of room for a fourth press," said Ingrid Solberg, the operations manager. "How orders are taken and handled will not alter, and no counter post will be lost."
The handover will proceed in three stages. In the first, beginning on 2 March, contractors will fit out the new building. In the second, from 20 April, company engineers will move the presses across, and although production will pause briefly, no order deadline will be affected. In the third, beginning on 1 June, the order collection point will transfer to Hollowbrook.
Ordering by telephone or through the online portal remains unchanged, as do current prices and counter opening hours. The one difference for customers is that from the third stage, finished work must be collected at Hollowbrook rather than on Wesley Street.
The firm also plans to hire 12 production staff. Applications close on 21 February and should be sent to its personnel office.

From: Lorna Beckett
To: All Third-Floor Staff
Date: September 30
Subject: Relocation to the Seventh Floor
Hello, everyone,
Our department has grown steadily this year, and to give everyone more room we will be relocating from the third floor to the seventh floor on Saturday, October 5. The move itself will begin at 8 A.M. Please complete the following before you leave on Friday:
1. Clear all personal items from your desk and cabinets by the end of the day on Friday, October 4.
2. Pack your belongings into the boxes provided and flag any fragile items with a colored sticker.
3. Label each box with your name and your new seat number.
Please note: The company will provide packing boxes, tape, and colored stickers at the third-floor reception desk. There is no need to purchase any of these materials yourself. I have also arranged for a professional moving crew to carry all furniture and equipment upstairs.
Finally, please reply to this message by 5 P.M. on Friday, October 4, to confirm how many boxes you will need, so that we can distribute them in advance.
Thank you for your cooperation,
Lorna Beckett, Office Operations Manager

HARTWELL (12 September)— The Hartwell Growers' Market is opening a second trading location to keep up with rising demand. — [1] —. Over the past year, the Saturday market has welcomed an average of more than 4,000 shoppers each week, roughly double the number recorded two years earlier.
The market has operated on Meadow Street for eight years, where 25 stalls sell fresh produce, baked goods, and crafts every Saturday morning. Organizers say the growth is largely the result of several new farms joining from the surrounding valley, which has widened the range of goods on offer and drawn visitors from neighboring towns.
To ease the crowding, a second market will open at Cranford Square, close to the town's central bus stop. — [2] —. The new site will run on Wednesdays and Thursdays from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., with room for up to 40 stalls, and sellers will pay a rental fee of 20 dollars per day.
"The weekday market means that people who work on weekends can finally buy fresh vegetables and bread from local producers," said Beatrice Nolan, director of the Hartwell Community Market Association. — [3] —. Samuel Ortega, who sells honey and preserves at the Meadow Street site, added that the extra days would help him reach customers he had never met before.
The association hopes to add a covered seating area for the colder months and is already considering a third location on the eastern edge of town. — [4] —.

Castleford Bike Share
Two Wheels, One City
Castleford Bike Share lets residents borrow a bicycle from one docking station and leave it at any other. Bikes are available around the clock at more than 40 docking stations spread across the city, and stations are checked and restocked each morning. Renting a bike takes only a few minutes, and the steps below guide first-time riders through a trip from start to finish.
How It Works
Step 1: Create an account online and choose a plan.
Step 2: At any station, tap your member card at the kiosk. The kiosk is run entirely by the app, so no staff are on site.
Step 3: Take the unlocked bike and ride wherever you like. The first 45 minutes of every trip are free, and longer trips add a small charge.
Step 4: Return the bike to any open dock and press the lock button to end your trip.
Membership is open to riders who are at least 16 years old. Registration is completed entirely online, and each member unlocks bikes using either the member card or the mobile app.
Report a Problem
If a bike is damaged or a dock will not release, open the app and tap the Report a Fault button to send us a short online form. Our team reviews these reports throughout the day. To recover a lost item, telephone the operations center during office hours.

Thornhedge Nursery Welcomes Visitors to Its Second Store
ARDENFORD (14 March) - Thornhedge Nursery, a family-run garden business known across the region for its wide selection of shrubs and flowering plants, has opened a second store on Wexley Lane in Ardenford.
The business began eleven years ago as a single stall selling potted herbs at a weekend market. Yvonne Castellan, who started Thornhedge and continues to oversee its day-to-day operations, said the company's steady growth had come from modest beginnings. "We had only a small table and a few dozen plants when we opened," she recalled. "Every step since then has been guided by what our customers ask us for, and this new store is the clearest sign yet of how far that has taken us."
The Ardenford store occupies a converted warehouse and features a bright indoor display hall, a covered courtyard for larger trees, and a separate room set aside for teaching. Wide aisles allow visitors to move easily between the seasonal arrangements, and a central advice counter is staffed throughout the day so that shoppers can ask about plant care before they buy.
The new location also introduces a program of hands-on planting workshops, something the first store was never able to accommodate. Sessions are held twice each week, and each one is limited to sixteen participants so that staff can give individual attention. Topics range from container gardening to the care of indoor foliage.
The store is open every day except Tuesday, from nine in the morning until six in the evening. General entry carries no charge, and throughout the opening month the nursery is offering each visitor a complimentary young seedling to take home.
"A garden center should be a place where people feel welcome to learn, not only to buy," Ms. Castellan said. "I hope this store gives our neighbours somewhere to spend an afternoon and to leave with something they have grown themselves."

Brayton Theatre Company Unveils Ambitious New Season
Regional troupe reports record attendance as it prepares to expand
MILLBROOK (July 18)—The Brayton Theatre Company will raise the curtain on its new season on September 12 with a fresh slate of six productions. Patrons are encouraged to reserve their seats without delay through the company's website at www.braytontheatre.org/season, where the complete performance schedule has been posted.
The announcement follows a period of remarkable growth. Attendance at Brayton performances has risen by roughly forty percent over the past four seasons, a trend the company attributes to its broadened programming and its lower ticket prices. "We have watched our audience grow steadily year after year, and this season is our way of thanking them for their loyalty," said artistic director Colette Ramsay.
To accommodate the larger crowds, Brayton will open a second performance space, the Pennington Stage, next season at the northern end of the Millbrook Arts District. Until that facility is ready, every production will continue to be staged at the company's existing home, the Aldridge Stage, at the southern end of the district.
----------------------

This season, the Brayton Theatre Company is introducing three subscription plans, each offering a different combination of tickets and benefits for the year ahead. Compare the plans below to find the one that suits you best.

Curtain	$60	Tickets to any two productions of your choice; a printed season newsletter
Encore	$120	Tickets to four productions; ten percent off any additional tickets; an invitation to the opening-night reception
Premiere	$220	Tickets to all six productions; an invitation to the opening-night reception; a guided backstage tour; priority reserved seating on the new Pennington Stage
To enroll, visit www.braytontheatre.org/season and enter the promotion code LAUNCH25 at checkout to lock in the introductory rate, which is available only through August 31. Subscribers who wish to bring companions may also add guest passes at $15 each. All reception guests are invited to gather in the lobby of the Aldridge Stage at 6:30 p.m. on September 12, before the opening performance begins.

Bracken Hill Conference Centre
We are pleased to tell members that reserving a meeting room at Bracken Hill is about to become far simpler. Our new online booking service, the ReserveHub portal, lets your organization view available rooms and request a booking at any hour of the day, without telephoning our front desk or visiting reception. The portal will open to all member organizations on 3 March. From that day onward, every meeting-room request must be made through the portal. Requests will no longer be accepted by telephone or in person at reception.
To secure a room, sign in to the portal using your member account, choose a room category and an event date, and then enter the number of people expected and the time slot you require. When you submit the request, the system records it and sends a confirmation summary to your registered email address, setting out the outcome of each request you have made. Catering and audio equipment may be arranged as optional extras at the time of booking.
Please submit each request at least five business days before the event date. Requests received later than this cannot be confirmed. Members may book rooms for up to forty people directly through the portal. Any event expected to draw more than forty people requires separate written approval from our events team before the booking will stand.
Any questions may be sent to the Member Services Desk. Please contact Devan Marsh at the desk for help with your account or with your first reservation.

questions.passage:
Foxglove Craft Supply Invites Shoppers to the Workbench
September 20 — For more than forty years, Foxglove Craft Supply has sold yarn, paint, clay, and countless other materials to the makers of Denbury. In all that time, however, the shop has never once offered guided classes of its own. That is about to change. Beginning next month, the store will run The Maker Sessions, a series of hands-on workshops in which shoppers can learn a new craft from start to finish and walk out with something they have made themselves.
Delia Faust, who manages events at the store, said the idea came from customers themselves. "People buy the supplies and then tell us they are not quite sure where to begin," she said. "We wanted to give them a place to sit down, try something, and leave with a finished piece they made by hand."
To introduce the program, Foxglove will hold a free preview afternoon on Saturday, October 5, when visitors can watch short demonstrations and ask questions at no cost. The paid sessions themselves begin on Saturday, October 19. Places are limited, and customers are encouraged to reserve a spot in advance, either through the store's Web page or at the customer desk.
----------------------
The Maker Sessions — Registration Form
Please complete this form to reserve your place at a workshop.
Name: Rosalind Pryce
Date: October 6
E-mail: r.pryce@brightmail.com
Telephone: (555) 0148
Please check your preferred session time (one only):
[ ] Saturday, October 19 — 10:00 a.m.
[x] Saturday, October 19 — 2:00 p.m.
[ ] Saturday, October 26 — 10:00 a.m.
[ ] Saturday, October 26 — 2:00 p.m.
Please rate your crafting experience (1 = I have never tried, 5 = very experienced):
( 1 ) 2 3 4 5
What do you hope to make or learn?
I would love to learn how to make my own scented candles to give as gifts. I have never made anything like this by hand before, so I am really starting from the very beginning.
How did you hear about The Maker Sessions?
My aunt has been attending candle-making and pottery workshops for years and is always talking about how much she enjoys them. When she heard that Foxglove was finally starting its own, she told me right away that I should sign up.
----------------------
The Maker Sessions: Fall Workshop Guide
Not sure which workshop to choose? The guide below sets out this fall's four sessions side by side, so you can see at a glance which one suits you best. Every session in The Maker Sessions includes all the materials you will need, so you can simply show up and start creating.
Session	What you make	Recommended level	Length
Hand-Poured Candles	Scented pillar candles	Beginner	90 minutes
Sculptural Candle Techniques	Layered decorative candles	Advanced	2.5 hours
Introduction to Pottery	A small clay bowl	Beginner	2 hours
Handmade Gift Cards	A set of greeting cards	Intermediate	90 minutes

Foxglove Craft Supply Invites Shoppers to the Workbench
September 20 — For more than forty years, Foxglove Craft Supply has sold yarn, paint, clay, and countless other materials to the makers of Denbury. In all that time, however, the shop has never once offered guided classes of its own. That is about to change. Beginning next month, the store will run The Maker Sessions, a series of hands-on workshops in which shoppers can learn a new craft from start to finish and walk out with something they have made themselves.
Delia Faust, who manages events at the store, said the idea came from customers themselves. "People buy the supplies and then tell us they are not quite sure where to begin," she said. "We wanted to give them a place to sit down, try something, and leave with a finished piece they made by hand."
To introduce the program, Foxglove will hold a free preview afternoon on Saturday, October 5, when visitors can watch short demonstrations and ask questions at no cost. The paid sessions themselves begin on Saturday, October 19. Places are limited, and customers are encouraged to reserve a spot in advance, either through the store's Web page or at the customer desk.

To: All Members
From: Louise Trevino
Date: 4 March
Subject: March skills workshop
Dear Members,
The Cadwell Business Association is pleased to invite you to our next member skills workshop, to be held at 6:30 P.M. on Thursday, 20 March, in the Marrick Conference Room at our main office. The session is free for all members, and no prior preparation is required.
What to expect:
A ninety-minute session on planning and managing daily operations
A guided exercise based on real workplace examples
A question-and-answer period with the presenter
A printed planning toolkit for every participant to take home
This month's session will be led by Desmond Attah, who served as operations director for eighteen years at Hartigan and Vale. Alongside that work, he co-runs a small print shop with his sister, and he gives three hours each week to the Bright Futures Coding Club.
To reserve a place, please reply to this message no later than Monday, 17 March, so that we can confirm seating.
Kind regards,
Louise Trevino
----------------------
http://www.summitskills.co - Meet Our Presenters
Interviewer: Welcome, Desmond. Could you tell our members a little about your professional background?
Desmond Attah: Of course. I spent nearly two decades as an operations director at a commercial insurance provider, where I was responsible for coordinating the daily workflow across several busy departments.
Interviewer: And where did your training begin?
Desmond Attah: I completed a diploma in business administration at the Corley Institute, which gave me a solid foundation long before I ever managed a team.
Interviewer: What will you focus on in your workshop for members?
Desmond Attah: I will show participants simple, practical ways to plan their working day and keep projects on schedule, all without relying on extra software.
----------------------
Bright Futures Coding Club
Do you know a young person who is eager to learn how technology really works? Join a growing program that helps them build genuine skills, one session at a time. Sessions run every Saturday morning throughout the school term.
How it works:
Open to students between the ages of 11 and 16
No experience or equipment required
Every student is paired with a friendly mentor
Places are offered on a first-come basis
Last year we welcomed more than 300 young people to our sessions. The Bright Futures Coding Club is run entirely by volunteers, and our aim is simple: to help young people in our community gain practical coding skills that open doors to future study and work.
To take part, or to offer your time as a mentor, sign up at www.brightfuturesclub.org.

From: Harriet Voss, Membership Coordinator
To: Trevor Aldington
Subject: Welcome to the Fernbrook Tool Library
Date: March 12
Dear Mr. Aldington,
Thank you for joining the Fernbrook Tool Library, a member-supported service that lends everyday equipment such as power drills, extension ladders, garden tools, and floor-cleaning machines. The library operates from a small workshop on Halbern Row in the Wexford district, and members may reserve items online at any time. The rules described below apply to every reservation, so please read them carefully before placing your first request.
Each item may be borrowed for a maximum of fourteen days, after which it must be returned or renewed. For every loan, we hold a refundable deposit equal to twenty percent of the item's replacement value until the item comes back, and items returned after the due date are subject to an overdue charge of two dollars per item per day. Because short loans require additional handling, any reservation covering fewer than three days must be approved in advance by a staff coordinator.
Your membership also carries several benefits. Members in good standing may borrow up to five items at one time at no additional charge, and every member receives one free equipment-safety workshop each year.
If you intend to collect your items outside our staffed opening hours, please make sure you have activated your locker access code before arriving, as our counter staff will not be present to assist you.
Kind regards,
Harriet Voss
----------------------

questions.passage:
From: Harriet Voss, Membership Coordinator
To: Trevor Aldington
Subject: Welcome to the Fernbrook Tool Library
Date: March 12
Dear Mr. Aldington,
Thank you for joining the Fernbrook Tool Library, a member-supported service that lends everyday equipment such as power drills, extension ladders, garden tools, and floor-cleaning machines. The library operates from a small workshop on Halbern Row in the Wexford district, and members may reserve items online at any time. The rules described below apply to every reservation, so please read them carefully before placing your first request.
Each item may be borrowed for a maximum of fourteen days, after which it must be returned or renewed. For every loan, we hold a refundable deposit equal to twenty percent of the item's replacement value until the item comes back, and items returned after the due date are subject to an overdue charge of two dollars per item per day. Because short loans require additional handling, any reservation covering fewer than three days must be approved in advance by a staff coordinator.
Your membership also carries several benefits. Members in good standing may borrow up to five items at one time at no additional charge, and every member receives one free equipment-safety workshop each year.
If you intend to collect your items outside our staffed opening hours, please make sure you have activated your locker access code before arriving, as our counter staff will not be present to assist you.
Kind regards,
Harriet Voss

Our website lists our full product range but is not used for workshop bookings.
We hope to see you there.
Warm regards,
Rowan Hill Homeware

questions.passage:
Made to Last: The Quiet Craft of Fairholme

By Adrian Colville

For more than thirty years, Fairholme has built a quiet reputation among people who care how a machine is made. Every model leaving its small workshop begins with a hand-brazed steel frame, a broad spread of gears for climbing and descending, and hand-laced wheels chosen for strength rather than weight.

Its founders remain sure that a frame built slowly will outlast several cheaper ones. Each joint is filed and polished before painting, and every finished frame is tested to be certain it can handle years of daily use on rough ground.

Fairholme makes no effort to court racers or weekend competitors. Its owners are the people who ride the same route to work each morning, carry shopping home each evening, and expect a machine ready to go in any weather.

One detail that longtime owners praise is the fully enclosed chain cover. By sealing the chain away from rain and grit, it saves riders from marking their clothes when they set out in ordinary dress rather than cycling gear. A built-in dynamo, meanwhile, powers the lamps, sparing riders the worry of flat batteries after dark.

Whatever the model, the goal stays the same: a machine that asks little and serves for many years.

42 Calderwood Street
12 September

Dear Ms. Ackroyd,
On behalf of the entire committee, I am pleased to inform you that Ackroyd Ceramics has been chosen as a finalist in this year's Pemberton Enterprise Awards. Being named a finalist is a significant honor, and the winners in each category will be announced during the ceremony itself.
Now in its ninth year, our program continues to celebrate outstanding local businesses. Nominations were submitted by members of the community and then reviewed by an independent selection panel. Nominations for this year closed in August. The finalists represent five categories: retail, hospitality, craft manufacturing, community service, and innovation. A cash prize will be awarded to the winner named in each category. Last year's overall winner, Foxton Leatherworks, will help present this year's awards.
The ceremony will feature a short talk by Bernadette Lowry. Ms. Lowry began her career in Canada before opening her own firm in our region, and she now devotes much of her time to mentoring young business owners. She has also announced that she will step back from her role as director of that firm next year.
The ceremony will be held on 18 October at Redmayne Hall, beginning at 6:30 P.M. A reception with refreshments will follow. Parking is available in the lot beside the hall. As this is an invitation-only event with limited seating, please confirm your attendance by 4 October.
Sincerely,
Malcolm Everhart
Awards Director, Pemberton Business Network
Telephone 555-0148 or e-mail awards@pembertonnetwork.org

https://www.larkfielddance.com/programs
Welcome to Larkfield Dance Studio
Since opening its doors in Cedar Valley, Larkfield Dance Studio has built its name on youth instruction. Every one of our current weekly classes serves students between the ages of six and seventeen, from first-time movers to competition-ready teens, and generations of local families have passed through our doors.
Meet Your Instructor
Lorena Bassett joined the Larkfield team last year. Before turning to teaching, she danced with several touring companies across South America, and for the past eight years she has coached adult learners at community centers, guiding people who arrive with no experience at all. Warm and patient, she is known for putting nervous newcomers at ease within their first lesson.
Our Space
Larkfield occupies a bright, ground-floor studio on Maple Row. Our two mirrored rooms can each comfortably accommodate up to thirty dancers, the floors are sprung for safety, and a small lounge just off the entrance gives waiting families a comfortable place to sit.
Starting Soon
This autumn we are opening a new evening course, Ballroom Basics, created for adults who are stepping onto the dance floor for the very first time. Beginning Monday, October 6, instructor Lorena Bassett will lead the group each Monday evening across an eight-week term. The term fee is $95. Places are limited, so early sign-up is encouraged.
----------------------
https://www.cedarvalleyliving.com/community
Grown-Ups Finally Get Their Turn at Larkfield
By Damon Whitby | Cedar Valley Living | September 22
For years, Larkfield Dance Studio has been a familiar fixture for Cedar Valley's youngest dancers. This October, the Maple Row studio is trying something rather different: a beginners' course built entirely for adults, and one that its organizers hope will draw people who assumed their dancing days had passed them by.
The eight-week program, called First Steps on the Floor, begins Monday, October 6 and will be led by instructor Lorena Bassett. Aimed squarely at people who have never taken a dance class of any kind, the course walks students through the fundamentals of ballroom dancing at an unhurried pace. Organizers are also quick to note that no partner is required to sign up.
"So many adults tell me they have always wanted to try this, but they were afraid of being the only beginner in the room," said Bassett. "This class is for exactly those people. Nobody here is expected to know a single step on day one."
The term costs $95, and registration is available only through the studio's website at www.larkfielddance.com.

To: All Staff
From: Trevor Osei
Date: February 24
Subject: New employee commuter shuttle
Hello everyone,
Beginning Monday, March 3, the Delmara Group will operate a morning commuter shuttle for staff, and I am pleased to say it will be offered at no cost to employees. The service was arranged to ease the pressure on our limited on-site parking and to give everyone a dependable alternative for the morning journey to work.
To reserve a seat, please register for one of the routes shown on the attached schedule no later than February 28. Seats on each route are limited, and they will be assigned in the order that requests are received.
On your very first journey, please show your employee identification badge to the route coordinator at the boarding point so that your name can be added to the daily passenger list. On every trip after that, the coordinator will simply check your name off the list before departure.
The attached schedule lists the boarding points that are available at launch. If none of them is close to your home, please write to our shuttle program administrator, who will look into adding a stop wherever there is enough demand.
Thank you,
Trevor Osei
Facilities Operations

Employee Commuter Shuttle Schedule
Program Administrator: Yolanda Pratt
Route	Coordinator	Departure	Boarding point	Seats remaining
Northgate Express	Gregory Lund	7:15 A.M.	Corner of Fifth and Main	3
Harbor Line	Simone Okafor	7:30 A.M.	Central Station plaza	0
Riverside Loop	Miriam Faulkner	7:45 A.M.	Willow Park entrance	6
Parkview Route	Raymond Tan	8:00 A.M.	Grand Avenue library	2
----------------------
To: Miriam Faulkner
From: Dennis Achara
Date: February 27
Subject: Riverside Loop enrollment
Dear Ms. Faulkner,
Following Mr. Osei's announcement about the new shuttle service, I have registered for the Riverside Loop and look forward to using it from Monday onward. I attended the short safety orientation for new riders yesterday afternoon at 4:30, so I am already familiar with the boarding procedure. Could you please confirm the exact departure time for the Riverside Loop, as I want to be certain I reach the boarding point with a few minutes to spare? I will also return my old parking permit to the security desk before the end of this week, since I will no longer need my reserved space.
Thanks,
Dennis Achara

To: Julian Prescott
From: Theresa Boland
Date: September 3
Subject: Venue proposals for the offsite meeting
Hi Julian,
Our annual staff offsite meeting is set for October, and we need to settle on a location soon. Harriet Blaine will be coordinating the site visits and confirming availability once we have narrowed the list down.
Please contact the candidate venues on our shortlist and request a formal proposal from each one, using the comparison you put together for last year's meeting as a guide. Forward each proposal to Harriet as it comes in so that she can begin arranging visits. Once they are all in, combine them into a single comparison sheet for me. I plan to include it in the recommendation I am submitting to the chief operations officer.
Thanks,
Theresa
----------------------
To: Theresa Boland
From: Julian Prescott
Date: September 15
Subject: Re: Venue proposals for the offsite meeting
Attachment: Venue Comparison
Hi Theresa,
The proposals are all in now. According to Harriet Blaine, four of the six venues we contacted returned a completed proposal, which is a stronger response than we had for last year's meeting. The figures are broadly in line with what we saw then, although Harriet did point out one surprise: the daily rate quoted by one of the venues came in well below all of the others.
The full comparison is attached. Let me know if you need anything further before you send it on to Ms. Calloway, or whether she would also like copies of the original proposals.
Julian
----------------------

To: Northgate Reel Rewards Members
From: Lorna Fitzgerald
Subject: Introducing Northgate Reel Rewards
Date: March 12
Attachment: Rewards Catalog
Dear Member,
Thank you for being part of the Northgate Cinemas community. We are pleased to introduce Northgate Reel Rewards, our new points-based program that lets you earn points on every ticket and concession purchase and exchange those points for a range of rewards.
All members begin at the Matinee level. At this level you earn one point for every dollar you spend, and you may redeem your points for any reward marked for Matinee members in the attached catalog.
Once you have spent three hundred dollars within a single calendar year, you are automatically moved up to the Marquee level. Marquee members earn two points for every dollar spent and may redeem their points for any reward marked for the Marquee level. They also enjoy one benefit reserved for this level alone: invitations to our members-only advance screenings, where you can watch selected films before they open to the general public.
To claim a reward, please review the attached catalog and confirm the points and level required for the item you want. Please note that each reward may be claimed only by members at the level shown beside it. Reply to this message with your choice, and we will verify your balance and arrange delivery or pickup.
Enjoy the show,
Lorna Fitzgerald
Membership Coordinator, Northgate Cinemas
----------------------
Northgate Reel Rewards Catalog
Reward	Points Required	Eligible Level	Delivery
Popcorn and drink voucher	200	Matinee	Collect at concession counter
Reusable beverage cup	250	Matinee	Collect at concession counter
Collector's film poster*	350	Marquee	Mailed to home address
Insulated travel tumbler	400	Marquee	Mailed to home address
Fleece cinema blanket	600	Marquee	Mailed to home address
* This reward is temporarily out of stock and cannot be claimed until it is restocked.
----------------------
To: Lorna Fitzgerald
From: Malcolm Reeves
Re: Introducing Northgate Reel Rewards
Date: March 15
Dear Ms. Fitzgerald,
Thank you for the information about the new program. I have been a Northgate member for about two years, and my account currently shows a balance of 450 points. Last month I attended one of the members-only advance screenings, which I thought was a wonderful benefit.
I would very much like to claim the fleece cinema blanket from the catalog. Could you let me know whether my current balance is enough for it, and, if it is not, which reward I would be able to claim instead?
Thank you for your help,
Malcolm Reeves

Posted March 2
Patrons visiting over the past week may already be aware that changes are underway at 82 Ferndale Lane. Following the landlord's decision not to renew our lease, and after several weeks searching for a suitable replacement site nearby, we have secured premises at 145 Kingsway Plaza, to which the business will transfer once renovations at the new site are complete. Regular service is scheduled to resume at the new address on March 24; the Ferndale Lane shop will cease trading after business on March 20.
Between those two dates no garments can be processed or released, since staff and equipment will be in transit. Customers are therefore asked to clear any outstanding orders from the current shop as soon as possible. Items remaining at Ferndale Lane after March 16 will be packed with the fixtures and moved across, causing a delay of several days before retrieval becomes possible at Kingsway Plaza. Collection at this stage remains free of charge, and staff will assist patrons in locating tickets.
Trading hours are unchanged — Monday to Saturday, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. — at both locations either side of the closure. Inquiries about individual orders may be directed to 555-0148 during shop hours, or to service@ferngatecleaners.com. We thank patrons for their continued support.

A Morning Well Spent at Larkspur Bakehouse
My neighbors had spoken about Larkspur Bakehouse for weeks, so last Saturday I finally stopped in to try it for myself, and I am very glad I did. — [1] —.
The almond honey scone was easily the highlight of my morning. It had been baked that same day, and you could taste just how much attention went into every layer. — [2] —. The coffee was rich and smooth, clearly prepared with the same patience.
Because the shop opened only a few months ago, word has spread fast, and the small dining room fills quickly on weekend mornings. — [3] —. There is only this one spot on Bramble Lane, and every order is placed at the counter, where you can pay by card.
My one small complaint is that the seating is very limited. — [4] —. So my advice to readers is simple: arrive early in the morning, before the crowd builds, and you will have your pick of the tables.

Introducing the Saturday Starters Program at Millhaven Swim School
We are pleased to announce a new weekend course for children who are learning to swim for the very first time. Beginning next month, the Saturday Starters Program will offer small-group lessons every Saturday morning for young swimmers between the ages of four and seven. The decision has not been taken lightly. For several terms our weekday beginner sessions have been running at full capacity, and each new intake has left a growing number of households hoping for a place we could not offer. Rather than continue to turn newcomers away, we have chosen to open a second slate of beginner places on Saturdays so that every child who wishes to begin can find one.
Millhaven has served local children for more than fifteen years. The school is led by head coach Rosalind Frayne, who competed at the national level before moving into teaching, and every instructor now on our pool deck was trained personally by Rosalind — including two colleagues she took on this spring — before taking charge of a class of her own.
Households already enrolled with us need do nothing at all. Weekday schedules are unchanged, existing bookings remain valid, and the online account through which you manage them will continue to work as before. The Saturday sessions are reserved strictly for children who are only now beginning to swim; current pupils should therefore stay with their weekday slot rather than transfer across. To reserve a place in the new program, please visit the enrollment page on our website or telephone the front desk at 555-0142. Places are limited and will be allocated in the order that requests are received.

options.label: C
options.text: Additional instructors have recently been hired.

Thornfield House Museum
Office of Volunteer Services
18 February
Ms. Deborah Ellison
27 Aldergate Road
Dear Ms. Ellison,
Thank you for applying to join the volunteer docent program at Thornfield House Museum. — [1] —. I am pleased to inform you that your application has been accepted, and we would be delighted to welcome you as one of our guides. We received a great many applications this year, and yours stood out for the enthusiasm you showed for the collection. When we spoke at our spring open day last month, you told me that your weekdays are free, and I am happy to confirm that the Tuesday and Thursday tour slots you requested are available. Our docents play an important part in helping the public understand and appreciate the history of the house.
During your first weeks, you will be paired with Frances Whitaker, one of our longest-serving guides. Ms. Whitaker has led tours of the house for the past nineteen years and is always glad to share what she has learned. She has kindly agreed to accompany you on your early tours and to help you prepare your own commentary for visitors. She is also well known for her talks on the restoration of the upstairs library. — [2] —.
Before you begin, there are a few steps to complete. Your orientation session is scheduled for Monday, 3 March, at 9:30 A.M. in the Garden Room on the ground floor. The session usually lasts about two hours, so please allow the full morning. During the session, new volunteers will meet the staff and see the areas of the house that are not open to the public. — [3] —. Please bring a form of identification so that we can prepare your entry pass. Once your orientation is finished, you may begin shadowing tours on the weekdays you have chosen.
If you have any questions before the orientation, please telephone our office at any time. — [4] —. We look forward to welcoming you to the team.
Sincerely,
Gordon Blythe
Volunteer Program Coordinator
Thornfield House Museum

Merrifield Observatory Opens Its Evenings to the Public
The Halbrook Public Observatory in Merrifield will launch a new after-dark viewing program, Starlight Evenings, beginning on 5 March. Running every week through the spring, the program invites residents to observe the night sky under the guidance of the observatory's staff rather than through a booked private tour.
Central to the program is a newly installed 400-millimeter reflecting telescope, the largest instrument the observatory has ever operated. It is the reason many residents will notice something new about the observatory this spring. Because it requires careful handling and darker conditions, the telescope is dedicated exclusively to the program's advanced deep-sky sessions. The introductory and family sessions will continue to use the observatory's smaller viewing scopes and its outdoor terrace.
"For years our finest equipment was available only to visiting researchers," said Dr. Rosa Meakin, the observatory's director. "This program is about opening those evenings to everyone in Merrifield who has ever wanted to look up and see more of what is there."
The launch comes at a time when chances for public astronomy in the region have grown scarce. The nearby Denholm Science Centre reduced its evening public hours last year following a review of its program spending, and the Ivelford Astronomy Club has since suspended its monthly open sessions, leaving few options for residents hoping to view the sky after dark.
Seats for each session are capped at 20 per evening, and the observatory encourages early booking. A full schedule of the spring sessions appears below.
----------------------
Starlight Evenings — Spring Session Schedule
Halbrook Public Observatory
Evening	Session	Level	Viewing area or equipment
Tuesday	Sky Basics	Introductory	Outdoor terrace, viewing scopes
Wednesday	Family Night	All ages	Main dome, viewing scopes
Thursday	Planet Watch	Intermediate	Main dome, viewing scopes
Friday	Deep-Sky Observation	Advanced	Main dome, reflecting telescope
Saturday	Constellation Walk	Introductory	Outdoor terrace
All sessions require advance reservation. Visit www.halbrookobservatory.org to reserve your place and to download session notes prepared for each evening's viewing targets.

options.label: A
options.text: To showcase a newly acquired telescope

options.label: B
options.text: To broaden public access to nighttime viewing

options.label: C
options.text: To reduce the observatory's operating expenses

questions.passage:
Protecting the Art You Love: Small Steps That Make a Difference

MARWICK (March 14)—A favorite painting or a framed family photograph can lose its color, and much of its value, faster than most owners expect. Living Spaces Monthly spoke with framing specialist Nadia Sorensen about the simple habits that keep artwork looking its best for decades.

Her first piece of advice concerns location. Never hang a picture where direct sunlight falls on it, she warns, because steady light will fade the colors within a few years. She also recommends keeping artwork out of kitchens and bathrooms, where changing humidity can loosen the paper and encourage mold.

The choice of materials matters just as much. "The single most important decision is the board placed behind the piece," Ms. Sorensen said. "Ordinary cardboard contains acids that turn yellow and stain the artwork, sometimes within months. Only acid-free board will truly protect it." She adds that the glass should be dusted gently and that frames should be kept well away from heaters and radiators.

Readers who would rather leave the work to a professional can visit Halden Framing Studio, which serves the Marwick area from its single location on Pinewood Row. Ms. Sorensen frames every piece with acid-free board, just as she recommends to readers. The studio does not deliver or operate branches in other towns; all framing is completed on site. Studio members are also invited to a free framing workshop held once a month.
----------------------

Membership and Collection

Halden Framing Studio has cared for artwork in Marwick for more than twenty years. This page explains how our membership works and how to collect your finished pieces.

Membership
For a yearly fee, members receive fifteen percent off all framing materials and an invitation to our framing workshop, held on the first Monday evening of every month. The workshop is open to members only and covers a different technique each session.

Collection
Finished pieces may be picked up at the studio from Tuesday to Saturday, between 10:00 AM and 5:00 PM. We are otherwise closed on Sunday and Monday. Please note that work left uncollected for more than twenty-one days will be charged a storage fee of five dollars per week. All pieces are mounted with archival board from Coleford Papers before being stored.
----------------------
Roland Mercer (9:02 AM): Hello, I would like to have a watercolor framed. I am interested in the Heritage package I saw on your site.

Gareth Pyle (9:05 AM): Good morning. The Heritage package is a fine choice, since it includes archival mounting and non-reflective glass. When can you bring the piece in?

Roland Mercer (9:07 AM): I will drop it off this Wednesday. One more thing, please add me to the list for next Monday's workshop.

Gareth Pyle (9:09 AM): Done, you are registered for Monday evening. Have you decided on a frame color yet?

Roland Mercer (9:11 AM): A dark walnut, please. When can I collect the finished frame?

Gareth Pyle (9:13 AM): It should be ready by the following Saturday. Remember that we take pickups until 5:00 PM.

Roland Mercer (9:14 AM): Saturday afternoon is perfect. Thank you very much!

MARWICK (March 14)—A favorite painting or a framed family photograph can lose its color, and much of its value, faster than most owners expect. Living Spaces Monthly spoke with framing specialist Nadia Sorensen about the simple habits that keep artwork looking its best for decades.

Her first piece of advice concerns location. Never hang a picture where direct sunlight falls on it, she warns, because steady light will fade the colors within a few years. She also recommends keeping artwork out of kitchens and bathrooms, where changing humidity can loosen the paper and encourage mold.

The choice of materials matters just as much. "The single most important decision is the board placed behind the piece," Ms. Sorensen said. "Ordinary cardboard contains acids that turn yellow and stain the artwork, sometimes within months. Only acid-free board will truly protect it." She adds that the glass should be dusted gently and that frames should be kept well away from heaters and radiators.

Readers who would rather leave the work to a professional can visit Halden Framing Studio, which serves the Marwick area from its single location on Pinewood Row. Ms. Sorensen frames every piece with acid-free board, just as she recommends to readers. The studio does not deliver or operate branches in other towns; all framing is completed on site. Studio members are also invited to a free framing workshop held once a month.
----------------------

Membership and Collection

Halden Framing Studio has cared for artwork in Marwick for more than twenty years. This page explains how our membership works and how to collect your finished pieces.

Membership
For a yearly fee, members receive fifteen percent off all framing materials and an invitation to our framing workshop, held on the first Monday evening of every month. The workshop is open to members only and covers a different technique each session.

Collection
Finished pieces may be picked up at the studio from Tuesday to Saturday, between 10:00 AM and 5:00 PM. We are otherwise closed on Sunday and Monday. Please note that work left uncollected for more than twenty-one days will be charged a storage fee of five dollars per week. All pieces are mounted with archival board from Coleford Papers before being stored.
----------------------

Meeting point: Rosewood Gate visitor pavilion
Party size: 3 adults

Please arrive at least fifteen minutes before the start time so that the group can set off promptly. Bring this confirmation, printed or on your phone, to the meeting point.
----------------------
Wrenford Gardens Introduces Guided Heritage Walks
WEXBRIDGE (14 February)—Wrenford Botanical Gardens will begin offering a new guided tour, the Wrenford Heritage Garden Walk, on 3 March. Places can be booked from this week.
The gardens were first laid out by Edmund Castellan more than a hundred years ago, when the grounds formed part of a large private estate. For much of the last century the land was closed to the public, and only in recent decades has it become a garden that anyone may visit.
The gardens are now run by their director, Bernard Mott. Visitors can enjoy a carefully restored greenhouse, a plant shop, and the Fernbank Café, all set within the grounds.
Each walk will be led by Margaret Ainsley, the gardens' senior horticulturist, who has cared for the grounds for many years and knows the history of nearly every planting along the route.
Later in the year, the gardens hope to add a series of evening walks for visitors who prefer a quieter time of day.
To reserve a place, visit www.wrenfordgardens.co.uk.
----------------------
★★★★
Wrenford Heritage Garden Walk — reviewed by Gerald Voss
I took part in the very first Wrenford Heritage Garden Walk on 24 March, and it was a delightful morning that I would happily recommend. Our guide, Margaret Ainsley, was full of knowledge and clearly loves the place. She led us along a winding route past the oldest trees and told us how the grounds had changed over the years.
The walk finished with complimentary tea and slices of cake in the Fernbank Café, which was a lovely touch. We also stepped inside the beautifully restored greenhouse, and the plant shop near the exit had a wonderful selection of seedlings to take home.

Date: April 3
Subject: Your group outing
Attachment: Booking form
Dear Ms. Ward,
Thank you for choosing Riverbend Indoor Recreation Centre for your company's team-building outing. Since opening our doors earlier this year, we have welcomed a steadily growing number of corporate groups, and we are delighted to arrange yours.
I have attached a booking form setting out the activities we propose. To make the best use of your time here, I would suggest that your group complete the registration and safety review through our online portal beforehand rather than on the day itself. I am keen to see that the team relay challenge, which is truly the highlight of the visit, receives the full time it deserves.
I understand that one of your participants, Martin Wexley, will be traveling and unavailable until early May. Even so, please confirm whether the proposed date suits the rest of your group.
Colin Baxter

Our Open Bench tier opens for enrollment this October. It is designed for returning students who have finished one of our beginners' or intermediate courses and want their own regular time at the wheel between the classes they take with us.
What's Included
Your $85 monthly fee meets the cost of up to 20 hours of self-directed studio time each cycle, along with use of every wheel, hand-building table, and shared hand tool on the floor. From: Terrence Ahmadi
To: Helena Voskamp
Date: 8 September
Subject: Your 14 October appearance — next steps
Dear Dr. Voskamp,
Thank you for accepting our invitation to speak at the North Ridge Logistics Forum on 14 October. --[1]--. I am pleased to confirm that your session, titled Cross-Border Freight in a Changing Market, has been scheduled for the second morning block of the program, from 10:15 to 11:00.
To support your presentation, our technical team will supply a laptop connected to the main projection screen, a wireless lapel microphone, and a printed set of handouts if you would like copies distributed to the audience. --[2]--. An honorarium of six hundred dollars — the association's standard rate for invited speakers — will be transferred to the account we hold on file within two weeks of the event, and a car will collect you from your hotel on the morning of the session.
So that we can prepare the program booklet and load the visuals in advance, please send a short biography of no more than 150 words together with a copy of your final slide deck by 20 September. --[3]--. If any images in the slides require permission from a third party, kindly note this in your reply.
It was a genuine pleasure to see you at our chapter dinner in Ellisport last April, when you had just returned from covering the shipping-line strike in Rotterdam. Several of our members are still asking about that assignment. --[4]--. I will write again in early October with the full program and travel details.
Warm regards,
Terrence Ahmadi
Program Director, North Ridge Logistics Association

Hollingford Recycling Program Opens Second Drop-Off Center
The Hollingford Recycling Program is pleased to announce that a second neighborhood drop-off center will open in Ferngate on Saturday, 11 October. The long-standing center on Marston Road will remain in full operation at its usual hours; the new Ferngate facility gives residents in one of the town's fastest-growing districts a nearby option for diverting everyday household materials. --[1]--.
The Ferngate center will accept paper, glass, metal, and rigid plastics. Weekend hours at the new site have been extended: it will be open from 8:00 A.M. to 6:00 P.M. on both Saturday and Sunday, several hours longer than the Marston Road location keeps on weekends. For a full list of accepted items and other general program information, please visit www.hollingfordrecycles.gov. --[2]--.
Visits to Ferngate can also earn credits through our new Recycler Rewards feature. To take part, register your household account on the program's website before your first drop-off. On each subsequent visit, scan the QR code posted at the entrance to log your activity. Accumulated credits may be redeemed at the customer counter for reusable containers and yard-waste bags.
During opening weekend, program staff will be joined by members of Green Hollow, which has organized neighborhood park clean-ups and monthly tree-planting outings across the district since 2015. They will guide first-time users through sorting and field questions about Recycler Rewards. --[3]--.
The program is inviting other neighborhood groups to apply as official collection partners. Partners host quarterly drop-off drives in their own area and receive materials-handling training from program staff. To learn more, call 555-0142 or submit an application at www.hollingfordrecycles.gov/partners. --[4]--.

Writing at Work: A New Weekend Series from Ardwick Learning Partners
Launching this autumn — a four-session Saturday program in business writing, designed for mid-career professionals.
Who this is for
This series is for managers, team leaders and specialists who have moved past their first promotion and now spend a large share of their week producing written material — reports for internal committees, proposals for external partners, project updates, and briefing notes for senior colleagues. If you write regularly for readers who are busier than you are, this series was designed with you in mind.
Background
Over the past year, several corporate clients approached us at the close of unrelated consultancy engagements to ask whether Ardwick could put together a structured business-writing course for their mid-career staff. We began sketching the program after those conversations, drawing also on feedback we had gathered from graduates of our earlier presentation-skills course and on broader concerns about writing standards across the sector.
What you'll do
Each session presents a specific writing challenge drawn from workplace practice. The first Saturday concentrates on the short internal report, examining how to lead with the decision the reader must make. The second turns to persuasive documents — proposals, funding requests, recommendations — and how evidence is best arranged for a skeptical audience. The third looks at correspondence with external clients, including messages that must decline or delay. The fourth session brings all three together in a full drafting workshop, with individual feedback from the lead facilitator.
The lead facilitator for the series is Ruth Farnsworth, formerly head of internal communications at a regional bank and a visiting lecturer in business writing at Ashvale University. The series runs alongside our long-standing one-to-one executive coaching service, which remains available separately.
Format and schedule
The series comprises four consecutive Saturdays from 9:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m., beginning October 18, at our Charter Street studio. Places are capped at twelve participants per cohort so that written work can be reviewed in detail. Preparation materials — short readings and a sample writing task — are e-mailed one week in advance of each session, and every participant receives a printed workbook at the opening meeting. An optional online follow-up module for graduates of the series will be released next spring.
A word from a returning participant
"I completed Ardwick's presentation-skills course two years ago and signed up for this the day it was announced. I trust the way the team structures a course — it always feels like time well spent." — Callum Beattie, senior operations analyst
How to enroll
Visit www.ardwicklearning.com/writing to reserve a place or to request the full syllabus.

questions.passage:
Writing at Work: A New Weekend Series from Ardwick Learning Partners
Launching this autumn — a four-session Saturday program in business writing, designed for mid-career professionals.
Who this is for
This series is for managers, team leaders and specialists who have moved past their first promotion and now spend a large share of their week producing written material — reports for internal committees, proposals for external partners, project updates, and briefing notes for senior colleagues. If you write regularly for readers who are busier than you are, this series was designed with you in mind.
Background
Over the past year, several corporate clients approached us at the close of unrelated consultancy engagements to ask whether Ardwick could put together a structured business-writing course for their mid-career staff. We began sketching the program after those conversations, drawing also on feedback we had gathered from graduates of our earlier presentation-skills course and on broader concerns about writing standards across the sector.
What you'll do
Each session presents a specific writing challenge drawn from workplace practice. The first Saturday concentrates on the short internal report, examining how to lead with the decision the reader must make. The second turns to persuasive documents — proposals, funding requests, recommendations — and how evidence is best arranged for a skeptical audience. The third looks at correspondence with external clients, including messages that must decline or delay. The fourth session brings all three together in a full drafting workshop, with individual feedback from the lead facilitator.
The lead facilitator for the series is Ruth Farnsworth, formerly head of internal communications at a regional bank and a visiting lecturer in business writing at Ashvale University. The series runs alongside our long-standing one-to-one executive coaching service, which remains available separately.
Format and schedule
The series comprises four consecutive Saturdays from 9:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m., beginning October 18, at our Charter Street studio. Places are capped at twelve participants per cohort so that written work can be reviewed in detail. Preparation materials — short readings and a sample writing task — are e-mailed one week in advance of each session, and every participant receives a printed workbook at the opening meeting. An optional online follow-up module for graduates of the series will be released next spring.
A word from a returning participant

Sincerely,
Dominic Halloran

To: Nolan Rivas
From: Claire Whitmore
Date: Wednesday, March 12, 9:40 A.M.
Subject: Lobby refurbishment quotes
Nolan:
The owners of Marchwood Center, Hessington Plaza, and Underhill Court have all approved lobby refurbishment work this quarter, and each site needs a written repair estimate from a pre-vetted contractor before I can consolidate a single recommendation to send back to the owners. Please reach out to three firms today and ask each of them for a full repair quote.
For the Marchwood Center lobby, please contact Renwick & Sons and ask them to pay particular attention to the cracked terrazzo flooring along the entryway. Talmadge Contracting should quote for Hessington Plaza, and I would also like you to arrange an on-site walk-through there so that their estimator can complete the reception-area survey he began earlier. Finally, Fossett Restoration's quote for Underhill Court should cover both the lobby floor and the reception desk.
All three written quotes must reach us by Friday, March 21, and the owners have set a firm ceiling of $12,000 per lobby, so ask each firm to keep its estimate at or below that figure. Please also note that Vernon Cade, our finance manager, will be traveling from March 18 onward and will not be available to review pricing during the second half of that window, so any figures that arrive late will have to wait until he returns.
Thank you again for the excellent work you did last month locating an emergency roofer for Underhill Court on almost no notice. I have not forgotten it.
Regards,
Claire Whitmore
Facilities Director
Halden Group
----------------------
To: Claire Whitmore
From: Nolan Rivas
Date: Wednesday, March 12, 1:20 P.M.
Subject: RE: Lobby refurbishment quotes
Claire:
I reached all three contractors this morning and can report back as follows.
Renwick & Sons will not be able to bid on the Marchwood Center lobby. Their operations manager told me the firm has just signed an exclusive maintenance agreement with Broadmere Property Partners and can no longer take on repair work from other property groups until that arrangement expires next year. I have removed them from the Marchwood file.
Talmadge Contracting confirmed within the hour. Their written quote for Hessington Plaza — $11,400, comfortably under the ceiling — arrived by e-mail just before noon, and I have booked their on-site walk-through for Tuesday, March 18 at 10:00 A.M.
Fossett Restoration is willing to bid on Underhill Court but, before it will commit to a price, has asked me to confirm whether the scope stops at the lobby floor and reception desk or also takes in the corridor lighting behind the desk. Could you send me your answer by 4:00 P.M. today so I can pass it on to them before their office closes?
Nolan Rivas
Administrative Coordinator

Ridgeway Camera Club Bulletin — Autumn Workshop Preview
Colette Ramsey Brings Night Landscapes to Ridgeway
By Sylvia Pemberton
September 12
Colette Ramsey, a landscape photographer whose long-exposure work has appeared in three regional gallery shows, will lead one of the two guest workshop tracks at the club's autumn weekend on October 18 and 19.
Her Night Landscapes track covers rural scenery from twilight through full darkness. Across the two evenings, participants will practice bulb-mode exposures, star-trail composition, and the handling of ambient light. All sessions in this track run after sundown, and the group meets outdoors on both nights.
Each registrant in the track receives a printed reference booklet on exposure settings, and everyone enrolled is entitled to a personal one-to-one critique session of half an hour with Ms. Ramsey at the close of the weekend. A sturdy tripod is required; remote shutter releases can be borrowed from the instructor for anyone who does not own one. Enrollment in the track is limited to twelve participants.

Hazelwood Kitchen
44 Palmer Street, Northwood
February 18
Dear Members of the Northwood Planning Board,
I am writing on behalf of Hazelwood Kitchen, which has leased the corner storefront at 44 Palmer Street for the past four years. During that time we have built a steady following among neighborhood residents, and we are grateful for the community's continued support of a small independent restaurant.
I would like to request a seasonal permit to place tables and chairs on the section of public sidewalk directly in front of our entrance from May 15 through October 15 each year. The proposed seating area would occupy approximately 120 square feet along the frontage of our unit and would accommodate roughly sixteen guests at a time.
In recognition of the impact this arrangement may have on people walking along Palmer Street, we are prepared to fund the installation of two planter barriers and a widened crossing marker at the nearest curb, according to whatever specifications the board considers appropriate. We hope these commitments demonstrate our willingness to share responsibility for the public space we would be using.
Sincerely,
Grant Holloway
Grant Holloway, Owner-Operator
----------------------
Northwood Planning Board
Meeting Minutes of March 11
In attendance: Chair Deborah Winters and all board members.
Approved items
• Member Naomi Draper submitted the final contract for the Palmer Street resurfacing project; the contract was accepted as read.
• Member Patrick Egan presented the revised quarterly budget for the department, which was approved without amendment.
• Member Simon Bhatt reported on the procurement of replacement office equipment for the municipal records room, and the purchase was authorized.
Discussion items
The board opened discussion on a request from Hazelwood Kitchen for a seasonal permit to place outdoor seating on the public sidewalk in front of its premises at 44 Palmer Street. Members raised questions about the width of the remaining walkway, the effect on the flow of people during the lunch hour, and whether an initial trial period should be attached to any approval.
When the floor was opened for public comment, Alicia Moreno, building manager of Chesterton Court at 42 Palmer Street, addressed the board in opposition to the request. Ms. Moreno stated that pedestrian traffic on the block is already heavy at mealtimes and that outdoor seating would make it more difficult for the residents of her building to reach their entrance and receive deliveries at the curb.
The board agreed to postpone a formal decision until its April session in order to review additional written comments submitted by Palmer Street residents.

To: Priscilla Osei; Damon Kroll; Beatrix Lemaire
From: Wesley Tanaka
Date: October 8, 9:12 A.M.
Subject: Copier lease shortlist — Truro branch
Team,
Following last week's tender review, which I ran on behalf of the department, I have shortlisted four vendors for the copier lease at our new Truro branch, which opens to clients in January. Please score each option against three criteria and return your comments by Friday: the monthly lease cost measured against the approved procurement budget, a print speed sufficient for the expected departmental print volume at Truro, and the on-site service response window. Our operations team has flagged the response window as the most sensitive of these, given the branch's distance from any regional service center.
The attached comparison chart sets out all four packages side by side. I will consolidate your scored responses before our meeting next Tuesday.
Wesley Tanaka
Cartwright Analytics
----------------------
Copier Lease Shortlist — Truro Branch
Vendor	Monthly Lease	Print Speed	Service Response Window	Installation	Standout Inclusion
OptiPrint Solutions	$340	42 pages per minute	3 business hours	On-site setup by vendor technician	Quarterly toner replenishment included
Northshore Office Systems	$295	55 pages per minute	4 business hours	On-site setup by vendor technician	Two staff training sessions included
Vantage Copier Group	$315	60 pages per minute	Next business day	On-site setup by vendor technician	Secure cloud scanning module included
Kestrel Business Machines	$360	48 pages per minute	12 business hours	On-site setup by vendor technician	Two-year replacement warranty included
All figures reflect the 36-month lease term negotiated during the tender.
----------------------
To: Wesley Tanaka; Priscilla Osei; Beatrix Lemaire
From: Damon Kroll
Date: October 10, 2:45 P.M.
Re: Copier lease shortlist — Truro branch
Wesley,
Thanks for pulling this together — I realize I am the last of us to send my comments back.
From here at the Halifax office, where we run two machines of the same class, I can tell you that any vendor that would leave the branch waiting more than four business hours for a technician simply will not work for Truro. The site is more than an hour from the technician base most of these vendors use, and a full day without a copier during month-end client billing has cost us real time before. Anything beyond that four-hour mark should be set aside regardless of price.
A higher print speed would also be welcome, since the new branch will absorb most of the client reporting we currently handle here, but I would treat that as a preference rather than a hard filter.
One further note: on total cost of ownership, the figure Priscilla and I have gone back and forth on most, her reasoning lines up closely with the criteria you set out, and it is worth circulating to the group before we meet on Tuesday.
Damon Kroll
Cartwright Analytics

Tired of waiting in line at a busy wash bay? Our crews travel across the Ferncroft area to clean your car exactly where it is parked. No trip across town, no long line, and no wasted afternoon.

Every wash is backed by a 48-hour satisfaction guarantee. If you are not satisfied with a wash during that period, our crew will return and re-clean your vehicle at no charge.
Booking is simple. Just call the number below to arrange a time. There is no form to fill out in advance, and no payment is required until the work is finished. All we ask is that you have an accessible parking space ready at your home so the crew can reach the vehicle. Our team arrives with its own water tank and equipment, and we supply all cleaning products ourselves and use them on-site, so nothing else needs to be prepared on your end.
Give your car the care it deserves without leaving home. Call today and book your first visit.

New Secure Bicycle Storage Room
Effective March 3 · Posted by Wrenfield Business Center Management
We are pleased to announce that the ground-floor bicycle storage room is now open to all building occupants. The room offers covered racks and improved lighting, and access is controlled by a personal entry code, so tenants no longer need to leave bicycles in the crowded outdoor lot.
To register for a personal entry code, please complete the following steps:
1. Visit the management office in Suite 100 during business hours.
2. Present the building access card that was issued to you when you moved in.
3. Provide the make and color of each bicycle you intend to store.
4. Sign the storage agreement and collect your entry code on the spot.
Once registered, occupants must observe the posted access hours of 6 A.M. to 10 P.M. and remove bicycles promptly if a rack is needed for maintenance. Please note that the room is monitored and that spaces are assigned on a first-come basis. Any questions may be directed to the management office.

From: Nolan Pierce
Subject: Designer recommendation
Date: March 12

Dear Angela,

You asked last week whether I knew a reliable graphic designer for your product catalog, and I am glad to recommend Curtis Holloway.

Curtis spent several years at Brookmere Creative Agency before opening his own practice. When I asked why he had struck out on his own, he explained that what he valued most was sitting down directly with the local business owners he served, rather than routing every decision through account managers. That focus is clear in how he operates today. He works almost entirely with small companies in our region, and he takes on several kinds of projects, including logos, printed brochures, and graphics for websites.

If you decide to reach out, Curtis offers a first meeting at no cost, so you can describe your project and view samples of his earlier work before committing to anything. You do not need to book weeks in advance, and the meeting is open to anyone considering his services, not only first-time clients. Once a project begins, he usually delivers the finished files within two weeks.

I engaged Curtis myself last quarter for our conference materials, and I was impressed from start to finish. When the completed booklet reached my supervisor, Ms. Loretta Vance, she was delighted with the result and asked who had produced it. That reaction alone should tell you a great deal about the quality of his work.

Please feel free to mention my name when you contact him. I am confident you will find him easy to work with, and I would be happy to answer any further questions.

Best regards,
Nolan Pierce

Account Tier: Priority

Order Status: Dispatched in full — 24 of 24 cartons
Dispatch Date: 3 March
Delivery Window: 5–7 March
Handling Terms: Accounts on our top service tier receive weekend delivery and a same-day dispatch confirmation at no extra cost. Accounts on the standard tier are limited to weekday delivery only.
Inquiries: For any question about this shipment, contact the dispatch desk at 555-0192 or reply directly to your account manager.
----------------------
From: Desmond Fairlie
To: Vanmoor Packaging Wholesale — Dispatch Desk
Subject: Regarding dispatch VP-40712
Hello Vanmoor Team,
I am writing to confirm that the 24 cartons listed on dispatch VP-40712 reached our main café on 6 March. Everything arrived in good order, the cartons have been unpacked, and the counts matched the notice exactly. Thank you for the smooth handover.
With that settled, I would like to sort out a few points for future shipments. First, please send all of our standing orders to our new central storeroom on Kelbrook Lane rather than to the café on Prentice Street. We have decided to hold all packaging stock in one place, and having it delivered directly there will save our staff a good deal of moving around. The storeroom is staffed from eight in the morning, so a delivery at any point during the day will be received without trouble.
Second, I wanted to ask about faster turnaround. During our busiest weeks we sometimes run low on cups with very little warning. If a same-week shipment can be arranged when that happens, could you let me know what such a request would involve and whether our account already covers it?
One last item to flag: please remove the wooden stirrers from our regular order. We have arranged those through a local supplier now, so there is no need to include them going forward. Everything else on the list should stay exactly as it is.
Thank you again for keeping our deliveries running so smoothly. I look forward to hearing how the storeroom change and the faster option can be set up.
Best,
Desmond Fairlie
Operations Manager
Thornbury Café Group
Direct line: 555-0148

Account Reference: New Enrollment — Maple Court Apartments
Attention: Ms. Renata Voss, Scheduling Coordinator
From: Gordon Selby, Property Manager
Date: 14 April
Subject: Setting up a recurring treatment plan
Dear Ms. Voss,
I manage Maple Court Apartments, a fourteen-unit residential building on Ashbury Lane. The property has never used an outside pest-control provider, but after comparing several companies I have decided that Hollowbrook Pest Solutions is the right choice for us, and I would like to open a regular service account.
Please enroll the building in the Steady Defense plan, which appears well suited to a property of our size. We would like the service to begin in May, and I would be grateful if the first visit could be scheduled for that month according to the day your plan already assigns.
The treatment should cover the following: ants and other crawling insects, rodents in the basement storage area, and wasp nests along the exterior walls. Several tenants have also mentioned the garden beds at the rear, so please treat those as a lower priority rather than a requirement.
Kindly confirm the arrangement and let me know the visit day tied to our plan. You can reach me directly on extension 218 during office hours.
Kind regards,
Gordon Selby
Property Manager, Maple Court Apartments
Direct line: extension 218
----------------------
Hollowbrook Pest Solutions — Residential Treatment Plans
All plans are carried out by licensed technicians and apply to buildings of up to twenty units. The rates shown below are effective from 1 March.
Plan	Frequency	Assigned Visit	Price per visit
Seasonal Shield	Every three months	First Monday, afternoon	$95
Steady Defense	Monthly	Second Wednesday, morning	$70
Full Coverage	Every two weeks	Thursday, morning	$55
Note: Every plan includes a complimentary termite inspection once each year. Optional mosquito fogging may be added to any plan for an extra $40 per visit.

Date: 12 February
Subject: Suite requirements for a preserves business
Dear Leasing Office,
I run a small business that makes fruit preserves, and I am ready to move production out of a home kitchen into a rented suite. Before arranging a visit, I would like to confirm a few requirements.
First, my recipes depend on a blast chiller, so the suite must include one. Second, I hope to begin production at the start of April. Third, I am prepared to sign for a full year, so a longer minimum term is not a concern for me.

Sincerely,
Miriam Foss
Owner, Wildfern Preserves
Retail shop: Bantry Street, Oldgate
----------------------
To: Miriam Foss
From: Declan Pryce, Leasing Team
Date: 12 February
Subject: Re: Suite requirements for a preserves business
Enclosure: Floor plan of the recommended suite
Dear Ms. Foss,
Thank you for setting out your needs so clearly. Weighing all three of your conditions together, there is exactly one suite that satisfies every one of them, and I have enclosed its floor plan so you can picture the space. That suite becomes available on the first of April.
Separately, I should mention that the Copper Loft will become free at the start of June, so if your production grows later in the year, a second space could be worth keeping in mind. One more thought: your retail shop happens to sit in one of the very districts we operate a kitchen in, so if staying close to your current premises ever appeals to you, we have a suite in that same part of the city.

Calderwood Timepieces Receives Northfield Design Prize
Award announced alongside the launch of a new collection
HAVENPORT, March 3, 2024 — Calderwood Timepieces reported today that it has received the Northfield Design Prize, an honor given each year by the Institute of Industrial Design to a single watch manufacturer. The judges praised the clean lines and lasting build of the company's Voyage model, noting in particular its clear, easy-to-read dial.
Founder Harriet Osei, who has personally overseen every watch design since she opened the company five years ago, said that the prize reflects the effort of the entire workshop rather than any single person.
Calderwood introduced its very first model in the year it opened, and that watch still sells steadily today. This month the company adds a new collection led by the Nocturne, its most recent design. As with every Calderwood wristwatch, the new models are designed and manufactured in-house, and the complete range is carried by retailers across the country.
Media inquiries: press@calderwoodtime.com. Contact: Harriet Osei, Founder.
About Calderwood Timepieces: Opened five years ago, the company builds durable everyday watches and sells them through independent shops nationwide.
----------------------
Model	Year introduced	Case size	Water resistance	Strap	Power source	Price band
Aurora	2022	38 mm	30 m	Leather	Solar	Standard
Coastal	2019	40 mm	50 m	Leather	Standard battery	Standard
Drifter	2023	43 mm	100 m	Fabric	Standard battery	Standard
Nocturne	2024	41 mm	50 m	Steel	Standard battery	Premium
Summit	2020	44 mm	100 m	Steel	Standard battery	Premium
Voyage	2021	42 mm	200 m	Rubber	Standard battery	Premium
Note: All models carry a two-year warranty. Final prices vary by retailer.
----------------------
Subject: Your recent visit to our service desk
Dear Mr. Delaney,
Thank you for bringing your watch to our service desk last week. Our technicians have cleaned the movement and fitted a fresh leather strap, and the piece is now ready for you to collect. Because your watch runs on light rather than a battery, there was no battery for us to replace. Please pick it up at the front counter between 9 A.M. and 5 P.M., Monday through Friday.
Best regards,
Owen Castleton, Service Desk Coordinator
Service reference: CW-3308
