Terrence,
Starting Monday, February 9, I would like the front desk to take over the evening handling of our early departure breakfast boxes.
Please keep a supply of cards at the desk, where blank cards are stored in the second drawer, and offer one to every arriving guest who reports a departure before the dining room opens at 6:30 A.M. Completed cards go in the tray beside the key cabinet. At 9:00 P.M., the tray should be emptied and the item totals telephoned to the night kitchen, which closes half an hour later, so that Roland Skoglund, our night kitchen supervisor, can pack and label each box overnight. Cards handed in after 9:00 P.M. cannot be filled, so please return them to the guest with an apology.
No card may list more than three items. Guests staying four nights or longer receive the box at no charge, and shorter stays are billed to the room at nine dollars. Any guest who wants a second box may buy one at that same rate and pay for it at the desk.
Thank you for taking this on.
Miriam Duclos

Issued by: Equipment Services Office, Sherborne Financial Services
Effective date: April 1
Supersedes: Schedule ES-4, issued in 2021
This schedule sets out the computing equipment allotted to each staff group and how often it is replaced. It applies to all staff at all company sites.
Group	Role description	Equipment allotted	Replacement interval
A	Staff working at one fixed desk	Desktop computer and monitor **	Every 5 years
B	Staff working at two or more company sites	Laptop computer *	Every 4 years
C	Staff visiting customer premises on most business days	Laptop computer and tablet *	Every 3 years
D	Staff sharing a workstation with a colleague	Shared desktop computer **	Every 6 years
* Portable equipment: the unit being replaced must be handed in at the equipment counter before the new unit is released.

From: Gillian Kaplan
Copy: Asset Register Section
Date: May 12
Subject: Equipment replacement now due (Schedule ES-6)
Dear Mr. Esposito,

Please confirm in writing, no later than May 23, whether a morning or an afternoon appointment during the week of June 2 suits you.
Sincerely,
Gillian Kaplan
Equipment Services Coordinator
Equipment Services Office
Extension 214
Group placements and replacement intervals are set out in Schedule ES-6.

District Business
Parcel Network Turns to Neighborhood Stores
By Bruce Sandoval
Hartwell Parcel Network will begin placing self-service parcel pickup units inside neighborhood shops this spring.

Midvale Business Review — Regional Business
Two Delivery Firms Now Operating as One
By Emmett Frawley, Winslow
The combination of Alderton Delivery Services and Halstead Transport is complete, and one operation now handles the scheduled deliveries and pickups that the two companies previously carried out separately for business customers in the nine districts they both served.
For more than fifteen years, both companies had sent vans into those districts on separate schedules. Neighboring streets were often served on different mornings, and customers in outlying areas waited noticeably longer than those close to either distribution center. Halstead Transport had also run Saturday pickups, which Alderton Delivery Services never offered.

For immediate release: February 18
Reduced-Rate Midweek Pickup Service for Smaller Business Accounts
BEXFORD, February 18 — Ravenscroft Linen Services announced today that a reduced-rate pickup service will be available to its business customers from March 2. --[1]--.
The reduced rate is offered to smaller business account holders, including guest houses, salons, and dental practices. Linen picked up on a Tuesday or a Wednesday is charged at 15 percent below the standard pickup rate, while linen picked up on any other day of the week is charged at the standard rate. No call to the office is required; an account holder selects the service on the account page of the company website. --[2]--.
"Our vans leave the distribution centers with space to spare in the middle of the week, and filling that space costs us very little," said Rachel Buckley, director of operations. "Crews and routes are the same on every pickup day, so a customer paying the lower rate receives the same service as before." --[3]--.
As an introduction, accounts on the reduced-rate service will also receive one additional midweek pickup at no charge through April 30. --[4]--. Standard rates for pickups on all other days of the week remain unchanged.
Media contact: Simon Ledbetter, 555-0148
Founded in 1994 with one laundry in Bexford, Ravenscroft Linen Services supplies laundered linen to business customers and now operates from eleven distribution centers across the region.

Rank	Requested block	Business days
1	August 4–22	15
2	July 14–25	10
3	September 8–12	5

Sincerely,

Cavendish Volunteer Center — Group Session Schedule
Sessions available: March 3 to March 28
Revised February 10
Send requests to the group bookings desk at groups@cavendishvc.org
Slot	Day and time	Activity	Places
V1	Tuesday, 9:00 A.M.–12:00 P.M.	Book sorting	12
V2	Tuesday, 1:30 P.M.–4:30 P.M.	Garden clearing	8
V3	Thursday, 9:00 A.M.–12:00 P.M.	Meal packing	9
V4	Thursday, 1:30 P.M.–4:30 P.M.	Garden clearing	8
Conditions for group bookings
1. Requests must reach the center at least fifteen business days before the chosen date.
2. Each group must name one contact person, reachable during every session booked.
3. Volunteers wear closed shoes and bring their own drinking water.
4. A consent card from the front desk must be handed in for each volunteer before the first session.
5. Volunteers must be sixteen years of age or older.

To: groups@cavendishvc.org
From: Elaine Lambert
Date: February 24
Subject: Group session request for March
Reference: February 10 schedule
Dear Group Bookings Desk,
I picked up your March schedule last week. Customers bring us lawn mowers and hedge trimmers that will not start, and our staff of fourteen puts them back in working order.
We would like the Thursday morning meal packing session in the week of March 23, and we can leave the workshop in the mornings only. Our whole staff wishes to take part, so please tell me whether there is room for all fourteen of us.
This request reaches you four weeks ahead of that week, which I hope is early enough. I will act as our contact person. My telephone will be on during each session. Everyone will wear closed shoes and bring drinking water.
Elaine Lambert
Owner
Wrenfield Works, telephone 555-0132
----------------------
Subject: Group session request
From: Curtis Underwood, Cavendish Volunteer Center
To: Elaine Lambert, Wrenfield Works
Sent: February 26
Reference: GB-1146
Action required by: March 13
Dear Ms. Lambert,
Thank you for the request recorded under the reference above.
Slot V3, the Thursday morning meal packing session, admits nine volunteers. Nine of your staff will therefore join that session in the week of March 23, and the remaining five will sort books in slot V1 on the Tuesday morning of the same week. Both sessions end at noon, which suits the mornings you are free.
Before the first session, please meet condition 4 on the group session schedule for each of the fourteen volunteers.
Sincerely,
Group Bookings Coordinator
Curtis Underwood
Office hours: Monday to Friday, 9:00 A.M. to 4:00 P.M. Messages left outside those hours are answered the next business day.

Around the City
Performers to appear in Woodgate Square
Four spaces have been set aside for licensed acts.
By Miriam Whitaker, March 12
Street performers will appear in Woodgate Square this spring under a new program run by the Woodgate Square Management Office. Counts taken last summer showed that the number of people in Woodgate Square fell by nearly half after the lunch hour. "Store owners nearby reported slow afternoon trade," said Miguel Ocampo of the office. Organizers say the shows should draw shoppers into the smaller streets behind the square.
Acts are grouped by category, and only one act from each category performs in a block. "The program is approved for one season only," Mr. Ocampo added. "If audiences grow, we will propose a second year." Allocations and conditions appear on the office's space allocation page.
----------------------
Woodgate Square Performance Program: Space Allocation
Last updated March 25
Program overview | Space allocation | Conditions of use | Contact
Act category	April 5 and 12	April 19 and 26	May 3 and 10	May 17 and 24
Music	Full	1 place	Full	Full
Theater for children	Full	Full	Full	1 place
Juggling and balancing	Full	Full	1 place	Full
One act only appears in each category per block. A category shown as full is offered the earliest later block with a place.
Setup: spaces open at noon. Performances run from 12:30 to 2:30 p.m.
Equipment: acts supply their own stands, seating, and sound equipment.
Power: an outlet is installed at Space 1 and Space 2 only. Acts at Space 3 and Space 4 must use battery-powered equipment.
Changes: ten days' written notice before a performance date.
Questions: spaces@woodgatesquareoffice.org
----------------------
To: Woodgate Square Management Office
From: Oliver Lombardi
Sent: March 28
Subject: Questions about our allotted space
Reference: Acceptance notice 4218
Attachment: printed conditions page
To the Space Allocation Desk:
Thank you for the acceptance notice. Lombardi Puppets has played at indoor children's parties for six years, but this will be our first season outdoors. Our show is a two-person puppet play for young audiences, and we hope to appear as early in the season as possible, so I would be grateful if you could confirm our dates.
The notice places us at Space 4. Our recorded music comes from a small player, and I would like to know whether an outlet can be installed there. As changes need ten days' notice, an early reply would help.
Oliver Lombardi
Manager, Lombardi Puppets
Please reply to this address.

Repair and Adjustment Services by Store
Current sheet; it replaces the one issued last spring.
Service	Lowden Street	Selwyn Road	Chesham Green	Ockley Bridge
Adjustments and screw replacement	While you wait	While you wait	While you wait	While you wait
Lenses installed in your own frame	Same day	By appointment	By appointment	Sent to workshop
Frame repair (hinges and broken joints)	On the premises	Sent to workshop	Sent to workshop	Sent to workshop
Weekly transfer day	Not applicable	Thursday	Thursday	Monday
Counter open until	6:00 P.M.	6:00 P.M.	8:00 P.M.	8:00 P.M.
Hand-in rule: items may be left at any store during opening hours, and the counter gives you a written record.
Full handling terms: see the notice displayed beside every counter.
----------------------
Local Shops and Services
Topic: broken frame, repair needed before a trip
Posted by Yvonne Pratt, 9:12 P.M., June 24
I have bought my glasses from Copeland Eyewear for years, always at the store nearest my apartment. It is the only one I can use, because I finish work at 6:30 P.M. and can never reach a counter earlier. The hinge on my frames snapped on Sunday.
I took them in this evening. The assistant explained that no repair work is done at that store. She said that items needing workshop attention are picked up once a week, on Thursday, so mine would wait until then. I leave on July 12 and do not want to travel with taped frames. Has anyone found a quicker route?
Y. P.
----------------------
Handling of Repairs Sent Off the Premises
For customers, effective from June 1.
An item left for workshop attention is entered on a record card at the counter and held in the store until the weekly transfer round. The case and the original receipt are not needed.
Stores without a workshop of their own send work out on one fixed day each week. Finished work returns to the store where the item was left, normally about three weeks later, and it cannot be picked up at the workshop.
No repair begins until the estimated charge has been approved. The workshop calls the number on the record card and waits for a reply. Payment is due at pickup, not at drop-off.
A customer who needs an item sooner than that may ask, before that store's transfer day, for it to be sent to the Lowden Street store by next-day courier. An extra charge applies.
Customer Care Office, Copeland Eyewear
A copy of this notice is displayed beside every counter.

Naomi Steiner

TO: All employees
FROM: Naomi Steiner, Administration Team
DATE: March 4
SUBJECT: Shared magazine subscriptions
Our nine shared magazine subscriptions end their twelve-month term in April, and each will continue only where recorded staff use justifies the cost. Copies circulate through the second-floor reading corner, and earlier issues remain available on request.
The decision will rest on a simple count: a title logged by six or more readers will be renewed, and any title below that figure will be withdrawn. Our administrative assistant will total the logs for the management team. No title has been dropped yet, and once decisions are announced, anyone who would like a withdrawn title reconsidered may write to me.
To make that count possible, please mark every title you have read this year on the log beside the shelves by March 21. If you have any questions, please call me at extension 342.
Naomi Steiner
Administration Team

Membership | Events | Annual Conference | Contact
Members are invited to propose a short presentation for this year's Annual Members Conference on May 9. All conference sessions will be held at Stonebridge Conference Center. The welcome dinner on the previous evening is held at the Riverbend Hotel. Any member in good standing may put forward one proposal, and only twelve speaking slots are available. Each proposal should be for one of the two presentation formats set out below.
Format	Length of slot	Suitable for
Short Talk*	15 minutes	A single practical idea drawn from your own work
Case Study Talk*	25 minutes	A longer account supported by handouts or slides
*An additional 10 minutes for audience questions follows every slot, whichever format is chosen.
To put forward a proposal, please follow these steps.
1. Send your proposal to proposals@lakemontrba.org, or leave a printed copy at the Hillcrest Street office.
2. Include the title, your chosen format, and a summary of no more than 150 words.
3. Make sure your proposal arrives by March 6.
Once the closing date has passed, the Conference Program Committee reviews all proposals together, and every member who submitted one is informed of the decision by March 20.
Page updated February 2. Questions about the conference may be sent to the Member Support Office at info@lakemontrba.org.

Larkfield Bookkeeping Services
Quotations Section
March 4
Ms. Rita Okafor, Owner
Pinehurst Cycle Repair
17 Alder Road
Re: Quotation Q-4127 for bookkeeping services
Dear Ms. Okafor:
Thank you for asking us to quote for regular support with your business records. This quotation covers your premises at 17 Alder Road, and the charges for the work are set out in the table below.
Item of work	How often	Monthly amount
Pickup of receipts and invoices from the client's premises	Every two weeks	$60
Entry of transactions into the account records	Monthly	$95
Preparation of a summary statement	Monthly	$70
Filing of processed papers in labeled folders	Monthly	$25
Total	$250
Two items are not included in the total above. The calculation of employee wages is charged at an hourly rate, and the correction of records prepared elsewhere is quoted separately.
Before we begin, please deliver your bank statements for the previous three months to us at least one week before the first pickup. Papers we pick up from you are sorted and entered at our own office and are then returned at the next pickup at no extra charge.
The amounts shown hold until April 30, after which a revised quotation will be issued. They are based on the frequencies listed in the table, and we would be glad to prepare a quotation for another pickup frequency on request. To accept, please sign a copy of this letter and return it to the Quotations Section by April 30, quoting reference Q-4127.
Sincerely,
Daniel Hart
Quotations Section
Larkfield Bookkeeping Services

The pipes that carry water to the upper floors are worn out and will be replaced next month. Each pipe feeds one group of floors, so the water will be turned off one group at a time. To see when your floor will be affected, check your floor group in the schedule below, which also names the restroom and drinking water point to use while your water is off.

Floors 2 to 4	Monday, May 5, 8:00 A.M. to 4:00 P.M.	Floor 6	Lobby station
Floors 5 to 7	Tuesday, May 6, 8:00 A.M. to 4:00 P.M.	Floor 3	Lobby station

- Drinking water in sealed containers at both substitute water points
- Cleaning of the substitute restrooms at midday and again at closing
- Signs at each elevator landing directing occupants to the replacement facilities
By 4:00 P.M. on the day before your group's date, please draw enough water for kitchen and cleaning use, since taps on your floor will not operate once the valves are closed. If your floor is not listed above, report the omission to the help desk at the extension below.

Subject: Outcome of your Workplace Borrowing Program application
Reference: WB-3072
Dear Personnel Coordinator,
Thank you for the application from Everdon Instruments for admission to our Workplace Borrowing Program. After reviewing it, we are able to enroll your organization for one year, and cards for individual employees can be prepared as soon as the remaining paperwork reaches us.
Two steps remain before borrowing can begin: please return the signed list of cardholders to this office, and arrange for one authorized employee to collect the cards in person at the Pelham Branch, the location designated for your organization. Both steps must be completed by March 14.
Your application asked for twelve cards. The number of cards available to a single organization differs from branch to branch, and the figure for your designated branch is shown in the attached directory.
You also asked about the training and careers section, which is not available at every branch. Cards issued at Pelham may be used anywhere in our service, so please use the directory to find a branch that keeps that section. Since your employees are able to visit only on Saturday mornings, please compare opening hours as well.
If anything in the directory is unclear, write to me directly.
Sincerely,
Neville Ibarra
Library Services Officer
Kirkstead Regional Library Service
Attachment: Branch Service Directory. Replies to scheme@kirksteadlibraries.org.
----------------------
Branch Service Directory
The entries below apply to organizations enrolled in the Workplace Borrowing Program.
Branch	Opening hours	Training and careers section	Staff cards per organization	Group visit arrangement
Weyburn	Monday to Friday, 9 A.M. to 5 P.M.	Available	10	Reserve the meeting room at least two weeks in advance.
Pelham	Monday to Saturday, 9 A.M. to 6 P.M.	Not available	8	Group visits must be booked with the branch manager.
Ingleton	Tuesday to Saturday, 10 A.M. to 7 P.M.	Not available	15	Confirm dates by e-mail three weeks ahead.
Radbourne	Wednesday to Saturday, 10 A.M. to 4 P.M.	Available	6	Group sessions need prior approval from the branch desk.
Staff cards are valid for one year and must be renewed at the branch that issued them.

questions.passage:
Fenmere Lake Boat Rentals — Equipment List and Charges
The list below applies to every canoe and kayak rental. Boats themselves are charged by the half day or the full day at the rates posted at the dock.
Item	Included with every rental	Daily rental fee	Visitor must bring
Life vest	Yes	—	—
Paddle, one per seat	Yes	—	—
Waterproof gear bag	—	$4.00	—
Wetsuit	—	$9.00	—
Roof straps for car transport	—	$6.00	—
Closed-toe water shoes	—	—	Yes
Parties of six or more must pay in full at the time of booking. Any rental started after 3:00 P.M. must be back at the dock by 6:00 P.M.
----------------------
Worth the short drive, and one charge I had not planned on
Posted by Rita Moreau
Rented: two-person kayak, full day
Rating: 4 out of 5
This was our third trip to the lake since early May, and my daughter asks for it whenever a warm weekend comes around. What brings us back is the staff. On our first visit neither of us had ever held a paddle, and the young man at the dock came out on the water with us to show us how to sit, steer, and turn back toward shore, without our having to ask. Besides the boat, the one thing I paid for at the counter was the extra layer they rent for cold water, which the lake in May certainly justified. I passed on the bag they rent by the day and left my phone in the car instead.
----------------------
I take out one of the canoes most Saturdays through the season, usually on my own, and these days I rent nothing along with it. For a full summer I kept paying the daily charge for the bag that keeps gear dry, then I added those charges up and found they came to more than the bag costs in a store. So for anyone who gets out here more than five or six times in a season, the sensible move is to buy that piece of gear and bring it along, and let the center charge you for the boat alone. I also keep an old pair of shoes I do not mind soaking in the trunk of my car, which saves a hunt in the parking lot.
Owen Guthrie
Canoe, most weeks in season
Fenmere Lake visitor comments board

questions.passage:
Fenmere Lake Boat Rentals — Equipment List and Charges
The list below applies to every canoe and kayak rental. Boats themselves are charged by the half day or the full day at the rates posted at the dock.
Item	Included with every rental	Daily rental fee	Visitor must bring
Life vest	Yes	—	—
Paddle, one per seat	Yes	—	—
Waterproof gear bag	—	$4.00	—
Wetsuit	—	$9.00	—
Roof straps for car transport	—	$6.00	—
Closed-toe water shoes	—	—	Yes
Parties of six or more must pay in full at the time of booking. Any rental started after 3:00 P.M. must be back at the dock by 6:00 P.M.
----------------------
Worth the short drive, and one charge I had not planned on
Posted by Rita Moreau
Rented: two-person kayak, full day
Rating: 4 out of 5
This was our third trip to the lake since early May, and my daughter asks for it whenever a warm weekend comes around. What brings us back is the staff. On our first visit neither of us had ever held a paddle, and the young man at the dock came out on the water with us to show us how to sit, steer, and turn back toward shore, without our having to ask. Besides the boat, the one thing I paid for at the counter was the extra layer they rent for cold water, which the lake in May certainly justified. I passed on the bag they rent by the day and left my phone in the car instead.
----------------------
I take out one of the canoes most Saturdays through the season, usually on my own, and these days I rent nothing along with it. For a full summer I kept paying the daily charge for the bag that keeps gear dry, then I added those charges up and found they came to more than the bag costs in a store. So for anyone who gets out here more than five or six times in a season, the sensible move is to buy that piece of gear and bring it along, and let the center charge you for the boat alone. I also keep an old pair of shoes I do not mind soaking in the trunk of my car, which saves a hunt in the parking lot.
Owen Guthrie
Canoe, most weeks in season
Fenmere Lake visitor comments board

Alan Chadwick

Denholm Power Equipment

To: All staff, Kingsley House
From: Gregory Paulsen, Site Services Manager
Date: October 6
Subject: Parking arrangements during resurfacing
Resurfacing of Halton Yard will begin on October 20 and continue until December 15. The affected section will stay closed for the whole period, leaving 96 of the yard's staff spaces in use. The separate visitor parking area is not part of the work and keeps all of its spaces.
For these weeks, on-site permits will be issued only to employees whose duties require them to drive during the working day. Until now, permits have not been limited in this way, and 180 were issued for the current year. Staff who do not meet this test will not be assigned a yard space, whatever their role.
Employees who are not entitled to a yard permit may instead use the leased lot on Ludgate Street, an eight-minute walk away, which holds 60 cars and costs $18 a month. Two other nearby places are not part of this arrangement: the visitor parking area, which remains reserved for visitors, and the public garage on Lomax Street, where the company has no agreement for staff parking.
Permits for the yard are picked up from the security desk on level one. A new permit will not be released until the current one is handed back, and no employee may hold more than one permit at a time.
Employees who believe their duties qualify them for a yard permit must submit a written request to the Site Services office by October 17. Any questions may be directed to extension 2650.
GP

Date: April 14
Subject: Viewing day preparation at Dalton House
Reference: VD-3140
Dear Site Team,
Our open viewing morning at Dalton House takes place this coming April 20, and the three vacant units need to be ready for visitors before the viewing day.
Unit 3 is our ground-floor retail space, so please wash down the storefront and set out the display boards at the front. Unit 6 is an upper-floor office space, and since the former tenant's fixtures are still inside, please clear the room and arrange the chairs for viewing. In Unit 9, our other upper-floor office space, please switch on the heating and check that every light is working.
One condition applies to the ground floor only: no ground-floor retail space may be opened to visitors until the completed fire-safety inspection certificate has been returned to this office.
Please send me a short note confirming that each unit is ready by 9 A.M. on the viewing morning.
Gail Hutchins
Leasing Manager
Kestrel Property Leasing
P.S. The keys for all three units are kept in the wall cabinet by the rear entrance.
----------------------
To: Gail Hutchins
From: Martin Deacon
Date: April 15
Subject: Re: Viewing day preparation at Dalton House
Reference: VD-3140
Copy: Leasing Team
Dear Gail,
Most of the preparation is now done, and I wanted to update you before the viewing day.
As always, I opened up each unit first thing this morning, went through them to check everything, and I have the keys with me. Unit 6 is clear and the chairs are set out, Unit 9 has its heating and lighting on, and I have washed down the storefront at Unit 3.
Even so, Unit 3 is the one space I have had to hold back. The ground-floor paperwork you mentioned still has not reached us, so I did not feel able to let visitors inside.
In its place, could we open Unit 9 to the people who had booked to see Unit 3? They could look around it during the viewing morning. Let me know before the 9 A.M. deadline whether that works, and I will adjust the list.
Martin Deacon
Dalton House
Reach me on site at 555-0176.

Host Enrollment
In the most recent round, the institute arranged supervised placements for 84 adult learners at 26 workplaces across the region. Offers of space met the demand for host sites for the first time in three years, and nearly every learner finished the full term.
Learner enrollment for the coming round is higher, so more host sites are needed. Any workplace that can give one learner routine duties for six weeks, with a named supervisor available throughout the learner's hours, may take part. The table below shows what the institute and the host site each provide.
Provided by the institute	Provided by the host site
Protective clothing and any equipment the learner requires	A named supervisor on site during the learner's hours
Insurance coverage for each learner while on placement	A work area and use of shared facilities
A coordinator visit in week two	A short written comment on the learner's progress
Host sites also give a brief safety introduction on the learner's first day.
To apply, a workplace completes the host form on this page and outlines the available duties. A placement coordinator then telephones within five working days to review the arrangements, after which the institute matches a learner and confirms the start date in writing. Host enrollment for the current round closes at the end of this month, and the next round opens twelve weeks later.
The program is supported by the Regional Skills Council. Questions can be sent to placements@pembrokeinstitute.org.

The Bulletin, Then and Now
Prepared by the Staff Communications Group

--[4]--. Material for each issue is due three weeks before its printing date and should be sent to Bridget Fitzgerald, who also gathers the photograph files and arranges each printing run with the outside firm. She can be reached at extension 3355.

Repaint your workplace without closing it for a single day.
We paint the interior walls, ceilings, and woodwork of offices, shops, and clinics that stay open through the day, but we do not offer outdoor work.
Our crews work in your building only in the evening. They start at 6:30 P.M., cover every desk and machine, and leave each room ready before your staff return the next morning. Evening work is arranged Monday through Friday only, and entry is agreed beforehand with your building manager. Because we use a low-odor paint from a specialist supplier, no smell remains by morning.
"I set the evening schedule for every crew myself, so no room is ever left unusable in the morning." - Trevor Baines
Before we can quote, we make a free estimate visit, which is offered to premises within 25 miles of our workshop and can be booked by calling 555-0161. To prepare, we need from you only a list of the rooms to be repainted, sent three days before the visit. At the visit, our estimator notes the condition of each surface for a written quote.

questions.passage:
Buildings and Design
The Firm That Chose to Keep
By Philip Grierson, Architecture Correspondent
When the city looked for a firm to reopen the Ravensworth Building, a 1911 structure that had stood empty for fourteen years, Tolliver Architects was already known for restoring a small chapel nearby. The firm won the job because its plan alone kept the front of the building as it stood. --[1]--.
The same care for the old building guided the work inside. The building's previous owner, a fabric merchant, had left the interior in place. --[2]--. Its original staircase and light fixtures were taken out and cleaned on the premises. These pieces were later reinstalled one floor above their original position.
"A building of this age never gives up all its secrets at once," says Naomi Wickham, the lead designer. --[3]--. Halfway through the work, the team found a sealed doorway behind a plaster wall and chose to repair and reopen it. Three panels missing from that doorway were the only pieces newly made for the project.
Today five businesses share the building's four floors. A café and a bookstore fill the ground floor, while the upper floors hold a publishing office and two design studios. --[4]--. The project has also been named a finalist for a national restoration award.
Members of the public may visit the building on Saturdays and Sundays from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., although booking is required. Groups of more than ten may request a guided tour by writing to tours@tolliverarchitects.com.
From the March issue of Belvedere Monthly.

Marbury Bus Terminal: Baggage Locker Service
Passengers who wish to leave baggage at the terminal may rent one of three sizes of self-service unit. Unit A suits shoulder bags and small cases, while Unit B suits travel bags and standard suitcases. Both are located on the main concourse beside the ticket hall. Unit C, which is intended for large suitcases and boxed goods, is found on the lower concourse by the platform stairs. The table below shows the largest item each unit will take, measured in any direction, together with the charge for each rental period.
Unit	Largest item	Up to 1 day	2 to 3 days	4 to 7 days
Unit A	45 cm	$4.00	$9.00	$16.00
Unit B	70 cm	$6.00	$13.00	$22.00
Unit C	100 cm	$8.00	$18.00	$30.00
Units may be opened only while the concourse is open, and passengers must clear their unit by closing time on the last day of their rental. Rental is charged by whole period, never by the day. Food, liquids, and valuables may not be stored in any unit.
Passengers may also leave baggage with staff at the Attended Baggage Counter, on the main concourse next to the waiting room, which accepts items of any size. Any piece larger than the Unit C limit must be reported to the counter two hours before drop-off, and the counter can be reached by telephone at 555-0128.
----------------------
To: Ms. Fiona Kaminski
From: Nathan Broadbent, Baggage Locker Service
Date: September 12
Reference: LK-3390
Copy: Attended Baggage Counter
Subject: Your baggage inquiry
Dear Ms. Kaminski,
Thank you for your message about storing baggage while you travel on from here. We can hold all four of your pieces, though not all of them in one place.
Your three travel bags fall within the Unit B limit, and one unit has been reserved in your name for the four days you will be away from the terminal. Although you quoted the one-day charge of $6.00 shown for that unit, charges follow the periods rather than single days, so your four days are billed as one period.
The remaining piece, a folding bicycle in a hard case, measures 130 centimeters. It must be handed in at the attended counter instead, and you will need to contact the counter yourself beforehand, as we are not able to do so on your behalf.
Sincerely,
Nathan Broadbent
Baggage Services Assistant
Baggage Locker Service
P.S. The attended counter takes items daily from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m.

Prospect Document Services
Copying and Printing
For many years our photocopying was sent to an outside supplier, which meant a wait of several days and a separate invoice each time. From this month the work is handled entirely within our own offices, and clients may order copies directly from us. Clients using the new in-house service can expect the following:
1. Our own staff run the copiers on site throughout our opening hours, so nothing you send us ever leaves the building.
2. You can follow the progress of every job from start to finish through your personal online account.
3. Finished copies are ready for pickup at our front counter on the same day they are ordered.
4. The account holder and anyone else named on the order may pick up completed work.
Two service levels are offered: Standard handling at $12 per order and Priority handling, for urgent work, at $30 per order. A minimum charge of $6 applies to any order of fewer than ten items. Account holders also pay a reduced binding charge of $4 when binding is added to any order.
To place an order, sign in to your account or call the order desk at 555-0192 between 8:30 A.M. and 6:00 P.M., Monday through Friday, when our offices are open. A member of the team will confirm your price before any work begins.

To: Subscriptions Desk, Trentham Call Answering Service
From: Judith Calloway
Copy: M. Sandoval
Subject: Service level inquiry [SI-2214]
Date: June 10
Dear Subscriptions Desk,
I manage a stationery shop alone and am away from the counter most afternoons, so many calls go unanswered. Since two other shops on my street use your service, I would like to subscribe as well, paying yearly in advance rather than monthly.
What I need:
(1) weekday calls answered until seven in the evening
(2) about 130 calls a month
(3) messages by text to my cell phone
(4) a professionally recorded greeting
Please tell me (1) which level fits a shop like mine and (2) how soon answering could begin. For any setup calls, I am easiest to reach before ten in the morning.
Judith Calloway
Owner, Hartwell Stationery
555-0134
----------------------
To: Judith Calloway
From: Warren Ludlow
Subject: Re: Service level inquiry [SI-2214]
Account: HS-3061
Date: June 11
Dear Ms. Calloway,
Your account has been set at the Extended level. This level covers the hours and the volume of calls you describe. Your yearly payment in advance has also been recorded. The professionally recorded greeting you requested is billed separately.
We will assign your shop a direct local number and draft your greeting text for your approval. We will then run a test call through your line on the morning before answering begins.
Your telephone line provider must set up call forwarding, as we cannot request it for you. Answering can begin only after that step is complete.
Warren Ludlow
Setup Coordinator, Subscriptions Desk
Subscriptions desk: weekdays until 6 P.M.

Pinehollow Outfitters
Everything for the trail, the campsite, and the road.
Welcome to Pinehollow Outfitters, the family-run store where you can find gear for hiking, camping, and outdoor travel of every kind.
Our four floors:
First Floor: Camping gear — tents, sleeping bags, and cooking sets.
Second Floor: Outerwear — jackets, rainwear, and casual clothing.
Third Floor: Footwear — hiking boots, sandals, and socks.
Fourth Floor: Wheeled Gear — bicycles, scooters, and carts.
If you plan to make a special trip in, please call ahead to confirm availability. Please also note that only items from our Outerwear range may be reserved through our website. All other stock must be viewed in the store before purchase.
Open daily from 9:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m.
----------------------
Free Gear Check-Up Weekend
Saturday and Sunday, November 8 and 9, 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
Bring in your bicycle, scooter, or cart for a no-cost inspection and adjustment by our trained staff. Items purchased elsewhere are welcome — you do not need a receipt from our store. Our team will check brakes, wheels, and moving parts, and make small adjustments on the spot.
If a replacement piece is needed, we can place a special order and have it shipped to your home address within two weeks, saving you the trip back.
This year, sessions will take place on the floor directly above our Footwear department.
----------------------
Perfect Stop Before Our Big Group Trip
Reviewer: Karen Sato
I've shopped at Pinehollow Outfitters twice this year and can't say enough good things. Each July I take a group of twelve visitors across the Pinehollow Ridge for five days on foot, and before this summer's trip we all needed matching rain jackets. We had tried three other stores that week without success. The staff here pulled options in every size we needed and let us try them on together. Everyone was outfitted in under an hour. I'll definitely be back next season when we need new boots.
Rating: 5 out of 5

First Floor: Camping gear — tents, sleeping bags, and cooking sets.
Second Floor: Outerwear — jackets, rainwear, and casual clothing.
Third Floor: Footwear — hiking boots, sandals, and socks.
Fourth Floor: Wheeled Gear — bicycles, scooters, and carts.
If you plan to make a special trip in, please call ahead to confirm availability. Please also note that only items from our Outerwear range may be reserved through our website. All other stock must be viewed in the store before purchase.
Open daily from 9:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m.
----------------------
Free Gear Check-Up Weekend
Saturday and Sunday, November 8 and 9, 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
Bring in your bicycle, scooter, or cart for a no-cost inspection and adjustment by our trained staff. Items purchased elsewhere are welcome — you do not need a receipt from our store. Our team will check brakes, wheels, and moving parts, and make small adjustments on the spot.
If a replacement piece is needed, we can place a special order and have it shipped to your home address within two weeks, saving you the trip back.
This year, sessions will take place on the floor directly above our Footwear department.
----------------------
Perfect Stop Before Our Big Group Trip
Reviewer: Karen Sato
I've shopped at Pinehollow Outfitters twice this year and can't say enough good things. Each July I take a group of twelve visitors across the Pinehollow Ridge for five days on foot, and before this summer's trip we all needed matching rain jackets. We had tried three other stores that week without success. The staff here pulled options in every size we needed and let us try them on together. Everyone was outfitted in under an hour. I'll definitely be back next season when we need new boots.
Rating: 5 out of 5

Notice of Renewal and Optional Space Offer
Reference: WB-4052
For ground-floor tenants of the Weybridge Building whose agreements end this quarter.
The adjoining suite has become vacant, as its former occupant moved to a larger site, and we are now offering it to current tenants before advertising it. The space is divided into three zones, which are shown in the attached plan.
Tenants may take the space on either of two terms. Under Option A, you would take all three zones for the full three-year term at the reduced rate given in your renewal letter. Under Option B, you would take the whole space for one year with the option to renew, although this option will proceed only if at least four tenants choose it. Under either option, heavy items may not be stored in Zone 3, as its floor cannot hold heavy goods.
Please deliver your written reply by December 5 to this office, which is open on weekdays from nine to five.
Leasing Administrator
----------------------

Zone 2 — Area: about 25 square meters. Access: through Zone 1 only. Partitions: can be moved. Services: power only.

----------------------
From: Bernard Pulaski
To: Gregory Maddox
Copy: Accounts Section
Subject: Reply to Notice WB-4052
Date: November 26
Dear Mr. Maddox,

I am glad to take the space, but I cannot commit the firm for the full three-year term. In addition, I can sign only after our senior partner returns from overseas in January, so I would ask you to confirm that the reception plan can proceed and to allow me more time to sign.
Bernard Pulaski
Office Manager, Trescott Legal Services, Suite 6

Trainee Department Manager Program — Pelham Supermarkets
Openings at four stores, including one that opened recently
Pelham Supermarkets invites applications from people who do not currently work for the company. Previous experience as a supervisor is not required.

Rating: 5 out of 5 stars
Title: A florist that truly delivers
Posted by Paula Reinhardt on March 18
I ordered flowers from Meadowgate Florist for a retirement celebration at my company, and I could not be happier. This was my first time using them. Gemma Fowler, a colleague in my department, spoke highly of the shop after her own event, and her praise alone persuaded me to try it. It is not the nearest florist to my office, and their prices were fair rather than the cheapest, but I trusted her judgment.
Their site advises placing large orders a full week ahead, yet they arranged mine with only two days' notice. On the day, they delivered the arrangement to my other office across town at no extra charge, which saved me a long trip.
When I called to swap the lilies for roses at the last minute, the staff took it in stride. The shop was plainly busy that afternoon, but nothing seemed to trouble them. Every stem was fresh, and the colors were exactly what I had described over the phone.
I will certainly use Meadowgate again. My colleagues kept asking where the flowers had come from, and I gladly gave them the name. In fact, I have already saved their number to book flowers for next month's staff anniversary event.

Please complete this form to join our introductory paddling program. The program is designed for adults who would like to try canoeing on the local river, and new members of every experience level are welcome. Return the form to the clubhouse desk by the end of the month.

To: Gregory Holt
From: Marion Whitlock
Date: May 20
Subject: Welcome to Cranleigh Canoe Club
Dear Gregory,
Thank you for registering with Cranleigh Canoe Club. We are delighted to welcome you to the paddling program.
We would like to invite you to an introductory session at the clubhouse. During the session, our instructors will cover the basic strokes, launching, and safety checks on calm water, so no prior training is needed. The session lasts around two hours and ends with refreshments in the clubhouse.
We have noted the request you made on your form, and everything will be ready for you when you arrive at the clubhouse. Please bring suitable clothing and shoes that can get wet.
Interest this season has been remarkably strong, and each session can take only a small number of newcomers at a time. For that reason, we will confirm your place by telephone as soon as a suitable date has been arranged.
We look forward to seeing you on the water.
Warm regards,
Marion Whitlock
Membership Coordinator, Cranleigh Canoe Club

Please complete this form to join our introductory paddling program. The program is designed for adults who would like to try canoeing on the local river, and new members of every experience level are welcome. Return the form to the clubhouse desk by the end of the month.

Preferred session:
[ ] Weekend morning group [X] Weekday evening group

Your paddling experience:
[ ] Never paddled before [X] Some experience, but not regular [ ] Paddle regularly

Do you need to borrow club equipment?
[X] Yes, I will need a canoe and paddle [ ] No, I have my own

Name: Gregory Holt
Telephone: 555-0137
E-mail: g.holt@westmail.example
----------------------
To: Gregory Holt
From: Marion Whitlock
Date: May 20
Subject: Welcome to Cranleigh Canoe Club
Dear Gregory,
Thank you for registering with Cranleigh Canoe Club. We are delighted to welcome you to the paddling program.
We would like to invite you to an introductory session at the clubhouse. During the session, our instructors will cover the basic strokes, launching, and safety checks on calm water, so no prior training is needed. The session lasts around two hours and ends with refreshments in the clubhouse.
We have noted the request you made on your form, and everything will be ready for you when you arrive at the clubhouse. Please bring suitable clothing and shoes that can get wet.
Interest this season has been remarkably strong, and each session can take only a small number of newcomers at a time. For that reason, we will confirm your place by telephone as soon as a suitable date has been arranged.
We look forward to seeing you on the water.
Warm regards,
Marion Whitlock
Membership Coordinator, Cranleigh Canoe Club
Reply to this message or call the clubhouse desk if your details change.

Lakeview Gifts — Service News
Posted August 1
Gift wrapping has been offered at our two stores for years. It can now be added to any order for delivery as well. For delivery orders, the charge is two dollars for each item wrapped, the same as in our stores. To mark the new service, we have also added two paper designs, bringing the choice to six.
How to add wrapping
1. On the order page, mark the box beside each item to be wrapped.
2. Pick your paper on the wrapping page, where all six designs are shown together.
3. Type your greeting in the message box. We print up to 100 letters on the card.
4. Check the full amount on the payment page before you confirm.
Tell us what you think: a feedback form follows every wrapped order.
----------------------
Lakeview Gifts — Wrapped Order Feedback Form
Customer: Lena Voss
Order number: 30947
Delivered: August 5
Please tell us about your wrapped order.
Choosing the wrapping was easy, and the parcel arrived on the day promised. Pricing was harder to judge. The wrapping charge did not appear until the payment page, after I had already made all my choices, so I could not see what I was paying for as I went. It should be shown at step two, while customers are still choosing.
The wrapping itself was excellent. It was even neater than the wrapping your staff did on the gifts I used to buy in person and collect at the counter.
[X] Please send me a reply
E-mail: l.voss@homemail.com
----------------------
Wrapped orders: fault at step three — Notice 6
To all packing room staff
Customers report that what they entered at step three of our wrapping guide has not been printed. A corrected file will be in use from August 12, and these entries will then be printed exactly as typed. Please note that the fix does not change where the charge is shown, which some customers have also raised.
Until then, write out each customer's step-three entry by hand from the order details, and enter the order number in the daily record. If a customer telephones the sales office to change an entry, the office will send you the new version in writing, and that is the version to use.
Send any question about a wrapped order to me.
T. W.
Tobias Weeks, Packing Room Manager

Reference: Custom Tumbler Order
Date: September 15
To: Nadine Kettering, Quinton Promotional Supplies
From: Lorraine Pryce
Dear Ms. Kettering,
Wrenfield Consulting will hold its annual staff gathering next month, and we plan to give every attendee a branded reusable tumbler as a keepsake. Having looked at the Cascade tumbler on your website, we would like to order 180 units in a single finish, each printed with our company logo. Could you also confirm whether an order of this size qualifies for the complimentary items listed on your product page? We would prefer to receive the shipment before the end of the month, so please send written confirmation and an expected dispatch date when you are able.
Sincerely,
Lorraine Pryce
Office Events Coordinator
Wrenfield Consulting
Direct line, extension 3352
----------------------
Home / Drinkware / Custom Tumblers / Cascade
Best-selling office favorite
The Cascade tumbler keeps drinks hot or cold for up to eight hours and carries a lifetime warranty against leaks. Each one is supplied in recyclable packaging. Its double-wall body is dishwasher safe, and your logo is printed directly onto the surface rather than applied as a removable sticker.
Unit price: $9.00 each
Available finishes:
FN-01 Matte charcoal
FN-02 Gloss white
FN-03 Brushed steel
FN-04 Soft sage
Bulk extras are available. Orders of 150 units or more include a complimentary set of spare lids, and orders of 300 units or more also include free on-site delivery.
Have a question about an order? Contact our order desk.
----------------------
Sender: Quinton Promotional Supplies
Recipient: Lorraine Pryce, Wrenfield Consulting
Ship-to: 22 Ellery Road, Weldon
Shipment reference: DN-6120
Dispatch date: September 26
Carrier: Overnight freight
Description	Finish code	Quantity	Status
Cascade tumbler, logo printed	FN-03	180	Dispatched
Storage cartons	None	6	Dispatched
Handling note: Please open all cartons within two days of arrival and report any damage or shortage to our order desk before signing the delivery record.

Valerie Musgrave

To: Valerie Musgrave
From: Calvin Lockhart
Date: May 20
Re: CV-3168
Dear Ms. Musgrave,
The second floor has changed the most. It now holds our reception desk and several meeting rooms, and visitors arrive in a steady stream from opening to closing. The fourth floor has been given over almost entirely to the storage of old records.

Calvin Lockhart

Subject: On-site fitting of replacement work boots
Dear colleagues,
Worn footwear is now the item most often reported to the safety team, which inspects the floor each month. Beginning this month, replacement boots will be issued here at the site instead of being ordered separately by each department. Tomas Bielecki will handle the fittings. Kimball Car Wash
Clean Finish Assurance
Every vehicle should leave our lanes looking the way you expected it to look. If the finish does not satisfy you when the wash ends, we will run your vehicle through a second time at no charge, with no change to our posted prices.
The assurance applies to all three of our wash tiers, including the least expensive. Basic Wash, Full Wash, and Deluxe Wash customers are treated alike, and holders of a monthly wash card are eligible as well. A repeat matches the tier originally purchased rather than a different one.
How to request a repeat wash
1. Speak to the attendant at the exit booth before you drive away.
2. Park in the marked waiting space to the right of the booth.
3. Remain with your vehicle until the second wash is finished.
Requests must be made in person at the exit booth and cannot be accepted by telephone. Please show the attendant the printed wash ticket issued the same day. The booth is staffed from 8:00 A.M. until 6:30 P.M., and the last repeat wash begins at 6:00 P.M.
Limits of the assurance
At any tier, the assurance does not cover interior cleaning appointments, which are reserved in advance by telephone, or the removal of tree sap and paint marks. Only one repeat wash is provided per visit.

Oakvale Driving School: Beginner Course
Home | Courses | Instructors | Enrollment | Contact
What has changed
Until last summer, a beginner's first lessons behind the wheel took place in ordinary road traffic, with other cars passing close by. Many beginners found those first lessons stressful. --[1]--. Those lessons are now held on a fenced practice ground away from public roads and reserved for our learners alone. This arrangement allows beginners to gain basic control of steering, stopping and turning before they encounter traffic at all. --[2]--.
How the course runs
The course is divided into three stages. In stage one, learners drive on the fenced ground only, in fifty-minute sessions with an instructor beside them. A stage two session on quiet local streets can be arranged only once an instructor has confirmed in writing that stage one has been completed. Stage three moves on to main roads and night driving. Learners who can provide proof of instruction received at another school are eligible to begin at stage two. --[3]--.
What we provide
A school car fitted with a second set of controls is supplied for every session, so no learner needs to bring a vehicle. In stage one, two learners share each car, taking turns at the wheel while the other observes. --[4]--.
Ready to start?
Complete the request form on our enrollment page, and the office will contact you to arrange a date for your first session.
Note: The fenced ground is closed to learners on Wednesday afternoons.

options.text: It allows any learner to begin on local streets.

Until last summer, a beginner's first lessons behind the wheel took place in ordinary road traffic, with other cars passing close by. Many beginners found those first lessons stressful. --[1]--. Those lessons are now held on a fenced practice ground away from public roads and reserved for our learners alone. This arrangement allows beginners to gain basic control of steering, stopping and turning before they encounter traffic at all. --[2]--.
How the course runs
The course is divided into three stages. In stage one, learners drive on the fenced ground only, in fifty-minute sessions with an instructor beside them. A stage two session on quiet local streets can be arranged only once an instructor has confirmed in writing that stage one has been completed. Stage three moves on to main roads and night driving. Learners who can provide proof of instruction received at another school are eligible to begin at stage two. --[3]--.
What we provide
A school car fitted with a second set of controls is supplied for every session, so no learner needs to bring a vehicle. In stage one, two learners share each car, taking turns at the wheel while the other observes. --[4]--.
Ready to start?
Complete the request form on our enrollment page, and the office will contact you to arrange a date for your first session.
Note: The fenced ground is closed to learners on Wednesday afternoons.

Review of Foxton Cleaning Services
Rating: 5 out of 5 stars
Posted by Delia Marsh, October 14
I run a small shop where customers browse the shelves before leaving with two paperbacks. It closes for only two hours each afternoon, and I refuse to shut out paying customers. Any cleaning had to fit into that short break. A cafe owner across the street recommended Foxton Cleaning Services, which mostly serves cafes and dental practices. The gym next door, however, suggested the Overnight Service.
Foxton offers four packages. The Maintenance Plan and the Overnight Service serve weekly clients and large sites. The Deep Refresh is a thorough cleaning lasting most of a day. The Express Clean is the quickest package and costs slightly more per hour than the Deep Refresh. Faster work, I assumed, meant weaker results, so the slowest package seemed best.
When I called, the staff suggested the Maintenance Plan, but I booked the quickest package instead. Having seen the prices, I was not surprised by its higher hourly rate. Although the Deep Refresh was available that week, I have not regretted turning it down.
On the day of the cleaning, the crew was gone before I reopened. The shelves were spotless, and the windows had not been so clear in years.
Looking back, I had the order exactly upside down. I will book the same package again but reserve it several days ahead, since same-day slots are rarely open.

To: All store managers
From: Cecilia Maddox
Date: July 28
Subject: Shelf sign replacement, SG-3418
Store managers,
Customers have told us that shelf prices are hard to read once they step back from the shelf. We are therefore replacing the signs in all our stores with ones that use much larger print, so that a price can be read from the middle of the aisle. The printed design, already the same in every store, will not change.
The larger size does affect some stores. Our older stores still use narrow sign holders, which the new signs will not fit, so a second, smaller carton of wider holders will be sent to those stores only.
The main cartons leave the supply center on August 4 and should reach you within a week. Each one holds a full set of aisle signs and a layout guide showing where each sign goes. All new signs should be in place by August 14.
Please do not throw away the signs you take down. The back of each old sign is blank, and next season's sale signs will be printed on that side.
Please send questions about missing signs to the Supply Desk and questions about delivery to the Transport Desk.
Cecilia Maddox
Sign Program Manager, Calder Stores
----------------------
SHELF SIGN REPLACEMENT - SG-3418
Delivery to: Calder Stores, Hopwell branch
This carton contains one set of aisle signs, 48 in all, together with one layout guide and one roll of double-sided tape. The wider holders are not included. They are sent separately, and only to stores that still use narrow holders.
Please have every new sign in place by August 21.
Count the signs against the layout guide before you start. If one is missing, write to the Supply Desk within three days of the delivery date. A sign reported later than that must be paid for.
Put the signs you take down in this carton and hand it to the next delivery driver.
Keep this sheet with the carton until the work is finished, then pass it to the store manager.

options.text: Shoppers cannot easily see prices from far away.

options.text: New sale prices will begin next season.

Around the Region
Museum Displays Head Out to Local Halls
By Alma Reichert
Ledbury Regional History Museum has extended its traveling display program to community halls and branch libraries across the district. "Most of these objects have never left this building," said Gordon Nasser, the museum's director of collections, "and the people they belong to should not have to travel to see them."
Each display travels in sealed crates and is delivered and collected by museum staff. Venues that take part agree to count visitors daily and report the total when the display is returned. Available displays are listed on the museum's Web site.
----------------------
Visit | Collections | Traveling Displays
Displays Available for Loan
Check each entry against your own room before requesting a display.
Display	Crates	Floor space	Maximum loan	Conditions
Village Schooling	2	55 square feet	2 weeks	●
Coins of the Valley	1	40 square feet	4 weeks	■
Valley Mills	4	100 square feet	4 weeks	●
Farm Tools and Harvest	2	45 square feet	4 weeks	●
■ Needs a room that can be closed and staffed during public hours.
● Needs a wall outlet near the display stand.
1. First-time borrowers are visited by museum staff before a display is sent. A venue that has hosted a display before may send current room measurements instead.
2. Each display is serviced for one week after every loan, and requested dates must allow for that.
----------------------
From: Ursula Wojcik
To: Traveling Displays Office
Date: October 9
Subject: Display loan for November
Attachment: Room measurements
Dear Traveling Displays Office,
Sedgefield Community Hall would like a display for the three weeks beginning November 18. Other bookings fill the hall before and after, so it must stay the full period.
Our display corner has 60 square feet of usable floor and wall outlets beside it, but no room here can be closed and staffed while visitors are present. I have attached our room measurements, so a survey visit should not be needed.
Our autumn talks concern the valley's mills, though any local subject would suit us. Which display can we take?
Ursula Wojcik
Program Coordinator
Sedgefield Community Hall
Messages reach me before 1:00 P.M.

Ledbury Regional History Museum has extended its traveling display program to community halls and branch libraries across the district. "Most of these objects have never left this building," said Gordon Nasser, the museum's director of collections, "and the people they belong to should not have to travel to see them."
Each display travels in sealed crates and is delivered and collected by museum staff. Venues that take part agree to count visitors daily and report the total when the display is returned. Available displays are listed on the museum's Web site.
----------------------

Valley Mills	4	100 square feet	4 weeks	●
Farm Tools and Harvest	2	45 square feet	4 weeks	●
■ Needs a room that can be closed and staffed during public hours.
● Needs a wall outlet near the display stand.
1. First-time borrowers are visited by museum staff before a display is sent. A venue that has hosted a display before may send current room measurements instead.
2. Each display is serviced for one week after every loan, and requested dates must allow for that.

Pinfold Community Sports Club, Fundraising Committee
January 22
To business owners on Sandbeck Road
Dear Business Owner:
Each spring our club holds a fair to raise money for equipment for our junior teams. --[1]--. About 900 visitors are expected this year. The fair includes a raffle, which is our biggest source of funds. To have enough prizes for such a crowd, we are asking each business on Sandbeck Road to donate goods, ideally unopened items in their original packaging. --[2]--.
A donation can be acknowledged in one of three ways. --[3]--.
Program listing: your name is printed in the event program and read aloud as each prize is drawn.
Website listing: your name appears on the club website through the month of the fair, then comes down.
Private thanks: nothing is made public, but the committee writes to you.
Mark one choice on the enclosed slip. Unmarked slips are treated as private thanks.
Small items may be left at the clubhouse office any weekday evening until February 7. For anything larger, call 555-0143 before February 13 and we will collect it. Label every item with your business name, whichever route you use. --[4]--.
Thank you for supporting our young players. Please call with questions.
Sincerely,
Ian Elliott
Raffle Coordinator, Fundraising Committee
Enclosure: acknowledgment slip
P.S. I collect the larger items myself, so expect a call to arrange a time. Committee work fits around my regular job, so collections take place in the evening.

To: All employees
From: Helena Eriksen, Personnel Officer
Subject: Staff discount program — online accounts
Date: October 3
The staff discount program is replacing printed discount cards with individual online accounts, and every employee must complete registration by Friday, November 14. Printed cards will be accepted in participating stores until November 28 but not after that date.
The change follows a review by this office, which found that printed cards were often lost or damaged. Gareth Vance, the Print Room supervisor, then ran a limited trial of the online accounts with his team from June to August, and no replacement cards were needed.
To register, follow these steps:
1. Open the staff services page and select the benefit account option.
2. Enter your employee number and your work e-mail address.
3. Choose a password and confirm the message sent to your inbox.
Staff will not need to go through this again.
Employees who are not assigned a computer can register with help at the reception counter on November 10 and 11. Ruth Zamora, who is responsible for the two evening shifts, requested this help because many employees on those shifts are not assigned one.
Account and password problems should go to the Systems Desk, extension 2214, and questions about the program to this office, extension 2260. The Systems Desk cannot correct the name on an account, so spelling errors should be reported to this office.

Diner Reviews
Reviewer: Corinne Hadfield
Rating: 4 out of 5 stars
Visit: weekday lunch, first time
For the better part of a year, a colleague named Delphine had urged me to try The Millstream Kitchen, and one recent weekday I finally gave in. The place sits a short walk from my office, though that was never what had kept it on my mind.
The weekday set lunch is the reason to come. Three courses arrive for a flat eighteen dollars, which is less than one main dish alone costs from the regular menu. I started with a squash soup, moved on to grilled river trout, and finished with a lemon tart.
Service was unhurried. A good stretch passed between each course, but I could happily have stayed at that table until closing. Sunlight came off the water through the tall windows, and the room stayed calm even as it filled.
One piece of advice: come early. I arrived just before noon and took what turned out to be the last free table by the water. Within half an hour, every riverside seat was gone. Sit anywhere else and you miss the best of the place.
Recommended for a first visit. Arrive early and ask for a riverside table.

For the better part of a year, a colleague named Delphine had urged me to try The Millstream Kitchen, and one recent weekday I finally gave in. The place sits a short walk from my office, though that was never what had kept it on my mind.
The weekday set lunch is the reason to come. Three courses arrive for a flat eighteen dollars, which is less than one main dish alone costs from the regular menu. I started with a squash soup, moved on to grilled river trout, and finished with a lemon tart.
Service was unhurried. A good stretch passed between each course, but I could happily have stayed at that table until closing. Sunlight came off the water through the tall windows, and the room stayed calm even as it filled.
One piece of advice: come early. I arrived just before noon and took what turned out to be the last free table by the water. Within half an hour, every riverside seat was gone. Sit anywhere else and you miss the best of the place.
Recommended for a first visit. Arrive early and ask for a riverside table.

Trade Floor
Machinery maker brings free demonstrations to three towns
Merrow Machinery Company has announced a series of free open demonstration sessions that will travel across the region this autumn, opening in Calderton on September 4. The company says the sessions are meant for workshop staff who want to keep their own equipment running well and to reduce the number of service calls they make to outside firms.
Each session covers routine cleaning, day-to-day safety checks, and the small repairs that operators can carry out for themselves. A company engineer leads every visit, demonstrates each task on a working machine, and takes questions from those attending.
The tour will stop in three towns on the following dates:
Date	Town	Venue
September 4	Calderton	Civic Hall
September 11	Redmarsh	Trade Center
September 18	Elsworth	Showground Pavilion
Admission is free of charge, but the number of places at each stop is limited, so visitors must reserve a seat in advance by telephoning the company's visitor desk.
Reported by Hector Vaughn
----------------------
To: Gerald Ashworth
From: Paulette Grimshaw
Date: September 2
Subject: Machinery demonstration in Redmarsh
Dear Gerald,
As you know, I will be traveling to our parts supplier just outside Redmarsh next week for a separate matter. It turns out that Merrow Machinery Company brings its free demonstration to that town on September 11, the very day I will be there, so I could attend rather than travel to an earlier stop nearer our Whitcombe office.
Would you be able to look over the topics the session will cover and mark anything you think our team should learn? I would really value your opinion before we agree on our maintenance plan for the year.
To make that easier, I will send you the printed demonstration leaflet later this week, so you can study the full list of topics well before our planning meeting on September 24.
Best regards,
Paulette Grimshaw
Facilities Assistant

Home / Business Services / Store Deliveries
Coverdale Delivery Company: Deliveries for Local Stores
How the service works
Each of our vans follows a set route through one group of streets, so the driver learns the area well. We collect goods from your store each afternoon and take them to your customers' homes, either before your store closes or after it has closed for the day. Our driver counts every item and checks it against your order sheet before it is loaded.
Requests for deliveries after store closing time have grown faster than requests for daytime delivery, and we expect this later demand to keep rising through next year.
Business line: 555-0198
Answered on weekdays, 8 A.M. to 6 P.M.
----------------------
Mapleton Furnishings, Trentham Street store: home delivery choices
Option	Area served	When to order	Charge
Standard delivery	Town center streets	By 2 P.M. the day before delivery	$10
Wider area delivery	Outer districts	Two days before delivery	$15
Evening delivery*	Town center streets	By 2 P.M. the day before delivery	$20
* Evening delivery is offered only from our Greenlaw store, which opened three months ago.
Staff check every item against your order before it leaves the store. Ask at the delivery counter to choose your option.
----------------------
Date: December 11
To: Mr. Iverson, Coverdale Delivery Company
From: Alison Thackeray
Subject: Taking over our customer deliveries
Reference: MF-2093
Dear Mr. Iverson,
Our store has taken purchases to customers' homes since it opened, using one van and one driver. Orders have risen sharply, and we can no longer reach every address on the day we promise.
We would like your company to take over these deliveries, and two points cover what we need. Deliveries should continue five days a week, and the charge for standard delivery should stay at $10. In addition, orders for standard delivery should be accepted until 10 A.M. on the day of delivery.
Please confirm by the end of next week whether both points are possible.
Sincerely,
Alison Thackeray
Store Manager, Mapleton Furnishings, Trentham Street store
Direct line: 555-0207

Evening language courses for working professionals
Courses run at four stages, from Stage 1 for beginners to Stage 4 for confident speakers. At every stage, a term is ten weekly evening classes, and study materials are included. At the end of each term, we send every sponsoring organization a progress summary for each enrolled employee.

Subject: Your Swim Course Enrollment
Dear Mr. Ackerman,
Thank you for registering at Selby Community Aquatic Center. Your place in our beginner group swimming course is now confirmed. The class meets every Saturday and follows the same routine each week, so newcomers can learn at a comfortable pace alongside others. Gareth Bowman works with the group in the water at every session, showing each movement before the swimmers practice it, while a lifeguard watches from beside the pool.
Please bring a towel, a swim cap, and a pair of goggles. Sessions usually start at ten o'clock, but the opening meeting begins an hour earlier, so plan to arrive by nine o'clock.
We look forward to seeing you.
Sincerely,
Naomi Pearce
Registration Coordinator

Sedgemoor Residents' Association
September 5
Dear fellow residents,
Over the past two months, residents suggested names for the new shared garden behind the community hall and then voted on a list of the most popular choices. Voting ended on August 31, and the results have now been counted. Thank you to the one hundred twenty-four residents who took part. The name that received the most votes is Primrose Green.
Now that the builders have finished their work, the garden is ready to open. We would like everyone to join us at Primrose Green for a short opening ceremony, followed by a tour of the garden. We will provide light refreshments, and there is no need to reply in advance.
We plan to hold the ceremony in late September or early October, most likely on a weekend afternoon. However, our committee has not yet chosen the exact day. We will send a second letter with that information, including the start time, as soon as it is decided.
Warm regards,
Howard Beckett
Grounds Coordinator

options.text: To report a decision made by residents

Local Business
Supermarket Chain Signs Agreement with Ockley Preserves
By Gordon Speight, Norcross, January 12
Supermarket chain Fulbeck Markets has agreed to stock goods from Ockley Preserves, a small company in Norcross that makes fruit jams, sauces and pickles in small batches, using fruit and vegetables bought from growers in the area. Its products will go on sale in eighteen of the chain's stores at first. --[1]--. These first stores are all in the south, and stores in other regions will follow later in the year.
Beatrice Tomlin, a former hotel cook, started the business six years ago by selling jars from a Saturday table she rented at an outdoor market in the town center. Within a year, a delicatessen two streets away became the first shop to take her goods. --[2]--. As more small shops began to order her jars, she rented a facility near the river three years ago, which is also open to the public for direct sales on Fridays and Saturdays. Buyers from the chain tasted the sauces at a food fair last spring and asked to see the facility.
"The smaller jar we prepared for the chain," Ms. Tomlin said, "is what I expect will bring us shoppers who have never bought from us before." --[3]--. The company has also taken on four employees since the fair, and a second large cooking pot has doubled the facility's weekly output. --[4]--.

Netherby Bank
Notice to Customers: Automatic Bill Payment
Customers who now visit the counter each month to pay recurring bills can have those bills paid automatically instead. The service is open to any holder of a personal checking or savings account at this branch.
To enroll, complete an authorization giving your name, account number and daytime telephone number, together with the company name and reference number of each bill you would like collected. For every bill, you may choose to have the payment collected on either the 5th or the 20th of the month. If the account is held jointly, the second holder must also sign the authorization.
Processing takes ten business days, and the arrangement takes effect only when our written confirmation reaches you by mail. Nothing will be collected before that date, and no bill on your authorization should be left unpaid in the meantime. Once the arrangement is in place, five business days' notice is needed to change or cancel the collection of any bill.
If your balance does not cover the amount due on a collection day, the payment will not be made and a fee of $12 will be charged to your account.
Completed authorizations are accepted only by the officer who handles account services at the counter, not in the lobby deposit box. Blank copies are available at the information desk in the lobby.

The Pelham Hotel
Conference and Events Office
Client Information Sheet CE-12: Preparation Duties for Single-Day Meeting Room Bookings
This sheet applies to all single-day bookings of our meeting rooms. So that each event runs smoothly, the preparation work is shared between the hotel and the client, and the table below shows each duty, the party responsible for it and the time by which it must be completed.
Code	Preparation duty	Responsible party	Completion timing
P1	Room layout and seating	Hotel	By 8:00 A.M. on the event day
P2	Name badges and attendee list printing	Client	Delivered to the events office two working days before the event
P3	Audio and projection setup	Hotel	Completed one hour before the start time
P4	Final refreshment numbers	Client	Submitted five working days before the event
P5	On-site equipment check	Client	30 minutes before the start time
Three of these duties carry further conditions. When confirmed attendance is 40 or fewer, the hotel will print the badges and attendee list at no charge, although folders for handouts remain chargeable. Refreshment numbers cannot be changed once the five-day deadline has passed, and the original count will be billed. In addition, the staff member carrying out the equipment check must attend a briefing at the events desk 15 minutes before that check begins.
Questions about this sheet may be directed to the Conference and Events Office.

Attention: Training Manager, Ingleton Systems
Dear Ms. Duvall,
Your seminar in the Tamworth Room on October 24 is confirmed for 38 guests. It was useful to walk through the room with you in September, and I am glad the space suits your program.
