Around the Table
Ten Evenings of Fixed-Price Dining
By Lionel Napier, dining correspondent
The Tarrington Dining Days program returns this year, opening on May 15 and closing on May 24. The event began on Tarrington Street and now reaches several side streets nearby. At each participating restaurant, guests may order a full dinner for one fixed price, with each owner choosing the dishes. The program is coordinated by Rosalind Ostrowski, who ran the district's summer street market for six years before taking on this event. "We would rather see guests try a restaurant they have never visited than return to a favorite," she said.
Ten evenings of dining are on offer, two more than last year. At Ms. Ostrowski's suggestion, the fixed-price menu has also grown and now runs to three courses rather than two.
The first of the ten evenings will be held at whichever restaurant joined the program most recently, and its owner will welcome guests at the door. For restaurant owners who wish to take part next year, registration is open until June 30.
A full list of the participating restaurants, the evenings they serve and the booking rules appears on the program's website.
----------------------
Tarrington Dining Days
2025 edition
Page last updated March 28
Home | This Year's Venues | Booking | Contact
Venue	Street	Evenings served	Year joined
Grove Kitchen	Tarrington Street	Six evenings	2019
Cypress Table*	Weatherby Lane	Ten evenings	2021
Two Lanterns*	Morley Court	Four evenings	2015
Sable Bistro	Bexley Square	Eight evenings	2024
Booking conditions
1. Each restaurant handles its own reservations. The program office cannot hold or change a table.
2. Guests must say that they are dining as part of the program when they reserve, so that the fixed-price menu is set aside for their table.
3. Tables for any evening of the program must be reserved no later than three weeks before the opening evening.
* These venues serve the program menu in a separate room.
Questions about menus or prices should be sent to the program office through the contact form on this page.

Spring edition of the Calderwood Business Directory
Preparing Your Entry
Who is listed. Every member business appears under one trade heading. Further headings may be ordered on the entry form.
How length is counted. Length is counted in printed lines once your text has been printed in the directory style, not in words as it was sent to us. The standard listing includes six lines. Checking. This office does not confirm the details members send in, and nothing can be changed once the edition has gone to the printer on March 10.

Jessop Tile and Flooring
Notice to Customers: Take-Home Sample Loans
Beginning March 2, customers may borrow samples of our tile, wood and stone products to see them in their own homes before ordering. The sample loan list below shows how many pieces of each type may be borrowed at one time, how long they may be kept and the deposit charged.
Sample type	Pieces per loan	Loan period	Deposit
Wall tile	4	7 days	$10
Floor tile	4	7 days	$15
Wood plank	3	10 days	$20
Stone panel	2	14 days	$40
Wall tile, floor tile and wood plank samples are collected from and returned to the sample counter. Because wood plank samples are kept at our storage building, please ask for them three business days in advance. Stone panel samples are not accepted at the counter, and a driver will instead pick them up from your address. The deposit is refunded in full when all pieces come back within the loan period, undamaged and in their case.
----------------------
Glad I borrowed them first
Rating: 4 out of 5 — service used: take-home sample loan
I wanted to see three narrow wood planks in my own hallway before ordering. They were not on the shelf when I asked, because that kind is kept in another building, so I came back later in the week.
I paid a twenty-dollar deposit that day. My installer then moved my installation date, and the planks stood in my hallway for sixteen days before I carried them back in their case. Nobody at the counter mentioned the date the planks were due back, and my deposit came back in full once the pieces were checked.
Ask for plank samples before you set an installation date.
Gwen Ainsley — would use again: yes
14 readers found this helpful.
----------------------
From: Miriam Dowsett
To: Owen Steadman
Cc: Sales Floor Team
Date: April 22
Subject: Loan period for samples kept at the storage building
Ref: SL-1408
Owen,
This concerns our take-home sample loan notice, in effect since March 2. May I have your approval to lengthen the loan period printed for the type of sample we keep at the storage building?
Borrowers say the printed period is too short, since that type takes several days to arrive at the counter. Meanwhile the counter has been returning deposits in full whenever the samples come back, with no charge for the extra days.
Only the loan period would change. Piece limits, deposits and the stone panel collection rule stay as printed.
Please reply before the notice goes to the printer on Friday.
Miriam Dowsett
Sample Counter Supervisor, Floor Coverings
Direct line 555-0146

questions.passage:
Jessop Tile and Flooring
Notice to Customers: Take-Home Sample Loans
Beginning March 2, customers may borrow samples of our tile, wood and stone products to see them in their own homes before ordering. The sample loan list below shows how many pieces of each type may be borrowed at one time, how long they may be kept and the deposit charged.
Sample type	Pieces per loan	Loan period	Deposit
Wall tile	4	7 days	$10
Floor tile	4	7 days	$15
Wood plank	3	10 days	$20
Stone panel	2	14 days	$40
Wall tile, floor tile and wood plank samples are collected from and returned to the sample counter. Because wood plank samples are kept at our storage building, please ask for them three business days in advance. Stone panel samples are not accepted at the counter, and a driver will instead pick them up from your address. The deposit is refunded in full when all pieces come back within the loan period, undamaged and in their case.
----------------------
Glad I borrowed them first
Rating: 4 out of 5 — service used: take-home sample loan
I wanted to see three narrow wood planks in my own hallway before ordering. They were not on the shelf when I asked, because that kind is kept in another building, so I came back later in the week.
I paid a twenty-dollar deposit that day. My installer then moved my installation date, and the planks stood in my hallway for sixteen days before I carried them back in their case. Nobody at the counter mentioned the date the planks were due back, and my deposit came back in full once the pieces were checked.
Ask for plank samples before you set an installation date.
Gwen Ainsley — would use again: yes
14 readers found this helpful.
----------------------
From: Miriam Dowsett
To: Owen Steadman
Cc: Sales Floor Team
Date: April 22
Subject: Loan period for samples kept at the storage building
Ref: SL-1408
Owen,
This concerns our take-home sample loan notice, in effect since March 2. May I have your approval to lengthen the loan period printed for the type of sample we keep at the storage building?
Borrowers say the printed period is too short, since that type takes several days to arrive at the counter. Meanwhile the counter has been returning deposits in full whenever the samples come back, with no charge for the extra days.
Only the loan period would change. Piece limits, deposits and the stone panel collection rule stay as printed.
Please reply before the notice goes to the printer on Friday.
Miriam Dowsett
Sample Counter Supervisor, Floor Coverings
Direct line 555-0146

From: Gloria Ackerman, Cranford Floral Studio
To: Andrew Sutcliffe
Subject: Confirmation of your weekly lobby flower service
Date: April 28
Dear Mr. Sutcliffe,
Thank you for arranging a standing weekly flower arrangement for the main lobby of your company. I am delighted to confirm that everything is now in place and ready to begin.
The white lilies you selected are a wonderful choice. They hold their shape remarkably well and will stay fresh for well over a week, so the display will look its best throughout each cycle. We have paired them with the seasonal greenery available this month.
Your arrangement will be delivered every Tuesday morning. The service itself begins during the first week of May, and each new display will replace the previous one.
Before that first visit, please make sure the reception area is left accessible so that our team can set the arrangement in place without any delay.
For the very first delivery, I will see to it personally, so please expect me at your reception desk that morning. I want to be certain that the display meets your expectations from the start.
Please contact me if you would like to adjust anything.
Sincerely,
Gloria Ackerman
Owner, Cranford Floral Studio

questions.passage:
A Small Room with Big Ambitions
Review by Nathan Puckett — 4 out of 5 stars
The Juniper Table, opened just this spring on Lowell Road, is the work of Imogen Fontaine, formerly head pastry chef at a celebrated city restaurant.
The dining room, redesigned by Helena Lawson, seats barely thirty and feels warm rather than crowded. --[1]-- Soft lighting and reclaimed wood give the small space real character. --[2]--
The savory menu is short but confident. Vegetables and herbs arrive each morning from Wickham Farm, a few miles away, and the kitchen shapes its dishes around whatever is delivered. --[3]-- The lemon tart, layered with impossibly thin pastry, is reason enough to book a table, and the warm chocolate custard is nearly its equal. --[4]--
For a room this small and this new, the cooking is remarkably assured, and I left already planning my return.
The Juniper Table, Lowell Road
Open Thursday through Sunday, from 5 p.m. to 10 p.m.
Reservations are strongly advised, as seating is limited.

Central Reservations Office
Reference: RS-4162
July 19
Ms. Renata Gallardo
12 Falmouth Street
Melrose
Dear Ms. Gallardo,
Thank you for your continued patronage. I am writing to inform you that guest rooms for travelers accompanied by a small pet are now offered at every Ludlow property.
The arrangement began at one property last year on a trial basis. Setting aside rooms there brought a steady rise in return visits from guests traveling with animals.
Each designated room carries a nightly surcharge based on the pet's weight, as shown below.
Category	Pet weight	Surcharge per night	Designated rooms per property*
Class 1	Up to 15 pounds	$18	4
Class 2	16 to 30 pounds	$26	3
Class 3	31 to 45 pounds	$34	1
*The counts above are the maximum at any property, and several smaller properties provide fewer rooms in Class 1 and Class 2.
Requests for a designated room are accepted by this office alone and should be sent to rooms@ludlowhotelgroup.com, although we expect to accept them through our online booking page as well beginning next year. Each request must state the pet's weight and must be received at least seven days before your arrival date. Please note that only one pet may be accommodated per reservation.
At check-in, you will be required to sign the pet care agreement presented at the front desk. Throughout your stay, pets must be carried or kept on a leash in the lobby and in all corridors.
Sincerely,
Tobias Solano
Reservations Manager
For general inquiries, please call 555-0163.

Revised Work Schedule — Calder Home Renovations
Project: KR-3820
Issued: June 12
For: Mr. Harlan Voss, 24 Larkspur Road
Dear Mr. Voss,
This notice replaces the work plan we gave you when your project began. --[1]--. Because an order has been delayed, the remaining stages have new dates.
Stage one (June 16–17): The crew will clear out your kitchen. This crew will handle every later stage too, as we never split a job between teams. --[2]--. Please be home at 7:30 a.m. on June 16 to let the workers in, but you need not stay.
Stage two (June 18–20): The crew will install the new sink and pipes and leave care instructions for them. --[3]--. Please keep your driveway clear for deliveries on June 18.
Stage three (June 23–25, formerly June 21–22): The crew will install your new cabinets. This stage has moved because the cabinets are late, and it will start only after they arrive. Please clear the dining area beside the kitchen by June 22 so they can be unpacked there.
Stage four (June 26–27): Our own crew will paint and remove all waste, using protective covering at no extra charge. This stage now takes two days instead of five, so the work will still finish on June 27. Our final payment request will follow it.
Please confirm you are ready the day before each stage. For stage three, we will instead contact you to confirm the start once the cabinets arrive. --[4]--. Please make any changes through our office, not with the workers.
Sincerely,
Bernard Chappell
Projects Supervisor
Office hours: 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., weekdays
Phone: 555-0146

Eastcote Community Gallery
Open Exhibition: Entry Confirmation
Thank you, Denise Aguilar. Your entry was received on January 24, and the works you submitted are listed below.
Title	Medium	Longest dimension
Harbor Morning	Oil on canvas	145 centimeters
Two Chairs	Watercolor	55 centimeters
You requested Section A for both works.
You asked to have your works listed in the exhibition catalog, and you told us that you will not need help carrying them in on hand-in day. You also confirmed that you will collect your works yourself after the exhibition closes, as every entrant must do within ten days of closing.
Please note the other conditions of entry. No entrant may submit more than two works in one year, and all works must arrive framed and ready to hang. Each work is shown in the section whose size range includes its longest side, and it is handed in only on the day listed for that section in the table below.
Section	Longest dimension	Hand-in day
A	Up to 70 centimeters	February 14
B	71 to 120 centimeters	February 16
C	121 to 180 centimeters	February 17
----------------------
To: Denise Aguilar
From: Owen Pritchard
Date: January 26
Subject: Open exhibition entry
Reference: Your online entry confirmation of January 24
Dear Ms. Aguilar,
Thank you for your entry, received here on January 24. Both works you listed have been accepted, and the change described below affects only one of them.
That work cannot be shown in the section you requested. Its longest side measures more than 120 centimeters, so it has been placed in the section for works of that size, and its hand-in day therefore changes. Please check the day shown for that section in the table on your confirmation page, and deliver the work on that day only.
Because you asked for a catalog listing, please also secure a typed caption card to the back of each frame.
Please confirm these arrangements by February 6. If you do not, the work will be held for a later exhibition.
Owen Pritchard
Exhibitions Officer
Eastcote Community Gallery
Desk hours 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., Tuesday to Friday. Telephone 555-0223, extension 18.

Trentham Stores, Supplier Standards Office
Reference: SS-3190 — Quarter reviewed: July to September
October 21
Mr. Simon Radcliffe, Orders Office, Pomeroy Provisions
Re: Delivery review, July to September
Dear Mr. Radcliffe:
In our check of your July to September deliveries, one of your four product groups fell below the standard we set, which is that at least 95 percent of deliveries in each group arrive on time.
Your account has therefore been moved to our watch list from the October to December quarter. Full standing returns once your combined share of on-time deliveries stays above 97 percent for two quarters in a row.
In the meantime, you may either keep an agreed amount of extra stock at our warehouse, so a late delivery does not empty our shelves, or accept a monthly check of your deliveries until your rate recovers. Please reply by October 31.
Sincerely,
Frances Ballard
Supplier Standards Manager
Extension 2210
All replies must be sent to this office in writing.
----------------------
Subject: Trentham review — which step to take
To: Marjorie Weaver — Copy: Orders Team Leader
The letter from Trentham came today. Our standing drops from the October to December quarter, so we must send back our choice soon.
The group that pulled our figures down is the one whose deliveries you handle every week. The summary makes that plain.
What worries me is the busy autumn. When orders climb in those weeks, getting our on-time share above the level Trentham now asks for is much harder, and I doubt we could keep it there for as long as the letter requires.
Could we meet for half an hour tomorrow to settle which of the two steps to pick before the reply date? Please bring the summary so we can go through each group.
Simon Radcliffe
Orders Office
Extension 3350

questions.passage:
Practice News
Booking Your Visits Online
Nobody enjoys waiting on hold at eight in the morning, yet that is exactly when our telephone lines are busiest. To help, Pennington Veterinary Clinic has opened a booking page on its website, which lets you book, move, or cancel a visit yourself at any hour. The page has been open for testing since February 24.
From March 2, the page accepts new bookings for routine health checks and vaccinations. Until March 16, a change to a visit already booked must be made by telephone. From that date, the page handles changes and cancellations as well. Bookings for dental work and other planned treatment follow on April 6. A visit for an animal that must be seen the same day will never be booked on the page, so please telephone the front desk.
If you use the new page, please rate each step on the short feedback form in our client area.
Miriam Lombardo
Client Services Manager, Pennington Veterinary Clinic

Keswick Systems Expands With New Regional Center
By Gwen Hollister, Wexbury — March 12
Keswick Systems, the software company based in Wexbury, announced this week that it will open a new regional service center aimed at supporting its rapidly growing customer base throughout the Hadleigh market. --[1]--.
The facility will occupy several floors of the Trelane Complex in Tarnwick, roughly an hour's drive south of the company's main offices, and will handle technical support and account services for the entire region. --[2]--. "Placing a team closer to our clients allows us to respond to their needs far more quickly," said Gerald Thornbury, the company's chief operations officer, who has overseen the project since it began.
According to the company, the center is expected to create about sixty new positions during its first year of operation. --[3]--. Hiring will proceed in stages, with the first group of employees starting during the first quarter of next year and additional staff added by the third quarter. Renovation work at the building is expected to be finished shortly before the first employees arrive. --[4]--.

Keswick Systems Expands With New Regional Center
By Gwen Hollister, Wexbury — March 12
Keswick Systems, the software company based in Wexbury, announced this week that it will open a new regional service center aimed at supporting its rapidly growing customer base throughout the Hadleigh market. --[1]--.
The facility will occupy several floors of the Trelane Complex in Tarnwick, roughly an hour's drive south of the company's main offices, and will handle technical support and account services for the entire region. --[2]--. "Placing a team closer to our clients allows us to respond to their needs far more quickly," said Gerald Thornbury, the company's chief operations officer, who has overseen the project since it began.
According to the company, the center is expected to create about sixty new positions during its first year of operation. --[3]--. Hiring will proceed in stages, with the first group of employees starting during the first quarter of next year and additional staff added by the third quarter. Renovation work at the building is expected to be finished shortly before the first employees arrive. --[4]--.

To: Ms. Imelda Garrick
From: Gordon Tolliver
Date: January 3
Subject: Certificate record CT-5109
Dear Ms. Garrick,
Your certificate for Customer Account Handling is now scheduled for printing. Please confirm the entries in your record before the batch is prepared.
When checking, please compare the name and course dates in the attached record with the enrollment form you signed on the first evening, since the attendance sheet from class was written by your instructor and often shortens names. We have already checked the course title against the center register.
Until January 8 your record remains open. After the batch has gone to print, a corrected copy carries a fee of $25 and adds about three weeks, because printing is scheduled only twice a month.
You may receive your certificate in one of two ways. It can be collected at our service counter, just inside the main entrance, on weekday afternoons from 1 P.M. to 4 P.M. between January 19 and February 20. Alternatively, we can mail it to the address of your choice, but only if you request this in your reply.
Please reply by January 8, confirming the entries or listing any corrections, and saying whether you will collect the certificate or have it mailed.
As you have completed your course, you may also enroll in a follow-up course at a reduced rate, an offer with no closing date.
Sincerely,
Gordon Tolliver
Records Officer, Kilbourne Training Center
P.S. We understand you will be working outside the area from January 12 until the spring, and we wanted to mention this before you reply.

Ulverton Hotel — airport transfer change, Room 306
Judith, Front Desk (10:42 a.m.): The guest in Room 306 left this note: "The four o'clock car leaves later than I need. Is an earlier ride possible?" Can the one-thirty van take one more passenger? I'm at the front desk until noon.
Fabian, Transport Desk (10:45 a.m.): The one-thirty van is shared, and it stops at the train station on the way. It leaves two and a half hours before her booked car. It holds eight passengers, and seven seats are taken.
Antonia, Duty Manager (10:47 a.m.): Her booking is the private car at four, isn't it? Another guest could use it instead.
Fabian, Transport Desk (10:49 a.m.): Yes, that car is hers alone. The van driver must hear about any addition at least an hour before departure.
Judith, Front Desk (10:52 a.m.): Then let me move her to the van now.
Antonia, Duty Manager (10:54 a.m.): Let's slow down there.
Judith, Front Desk (10:57 a.m.): Fair enough. She stopped by the desk, so I explained what the van involves. She accepts the earlier time and the extra stop.
Antonia, Duty Manager (11:00 a.m.): Good. Fabian, can you print the new departure details and take them up to her room? I will call the driver myself.
Fabian, Transport Desk (11:02 a.m.): Happy to. I'll be at her door in ten minutes.
Thread marked resolved at 11:05 a.m.

Rothwell Family Health Clinic
Appointment Reminder Messages
Effective November 12
Issued by the Appointments Desk
Reception staff currently telephone each client on the day before a scheduled visit. Because these calls take much of the morning at the front counter, they will end on the date shown above and be replaced by text messages sent to the client's phone. Clients who have told the clinic that they cannot receive text messages are not affected by this change, and reception staff will continue to telephone them the day before each visit. Clients who want the messages must join the service themselves, as no one is entered automatically.
To join, ask for a registration slip at the reception window, write the number the messages should be sent to, and hand the completed slip back to a receptionist. No other document is needed.
A message is sent five days before the appointment. It gives the date and time of the booking and the name of the staff member the client will see, and it states which room to report to on arrival. The message also asks for a brief reply confirming that the client still intends to come, and if no reply reaches the clinic by six hours before the appointment time, the slot is offered to another client.
Questions about the service may be directed to the Appointments Desk at extension 2705.

Hawthorn Apartments - Resident Handbook: Shared Facilities
Revised May 2
Residents may reserve the service elevator, the meeting room, and the roof terrace at no charge, and each reservation of any facility lasts two hours. Written requests must reach the management office five days ahead, and each apartment may hold one reservation per week.
Of the three facilities, the service elevator is the one residents reserve for a move, and the rules that follow apply to those reservations only. Before each one, building staff pad the elevator walls and lay floor covers between the entrance and the elevator, but they do not carry or pack belongings.
On the day of the move, furniture and large cartons may be taken through the basement loading door, which is staffed on weekdays only, so on a weekend reservation every item must pass through the main lobby. As for the elevator itself, the attendant on duty unlocks it for the first reservation of the day, while residents with a later reservation collect the elevator key at the management office counter.
The management office is open daily, 8:00 A.M. to 6:00 P.M.
----------------------

Nathan Boland

New terms apply from January 1
November 20
Ledbury Conference Center has completed work on its Kestrel Hall. The hall has been divided into three suites, Kestrel One, Kestrel Two and Kestrel Three, which may be reserved singly or combined. Oakmere Bakery
Every cake baked in our own kitchens
Whether you are planning a family dinner or a large office party, Oakmere Bakery has a cake to suit the occasion. Our cakes come in three sizes, which are set out in the table below.
Size	Serves up to	Top	Price
Small	Eight people	Plain top only	$22
Medium	Sixteen people	Fruit or plain top	$38
Large	Thirty people	Any design, including a written greeting	$60
Ordering
To order, choose your shop and your pickup day at the counter and pay half the price, and the rest is due when you pick the cake up. Because large cakes are baked at only some of our shops, please see our shop list before ordering one, and allow five days' notice for any large cake. To learn more, come in and talk to the staff at any of our four shops.
----------------------
Oakmere Bakery Shop List
Shop	Cake sizes baked here	Weekend opening time	Where orders are picked up
Priory Street	Small and medium	8:00 A.M.	Front counter
Church Road	Small, medium and large	9:30 A.M.	Side door
Eastcote	Small and medium	9:30 A.M.	Front counter
Overton	Small, medium and large	8:00 A.M.	Side door
* Pickups before opening time must be arranged in advance with Oscar Nystrom, the baker who starts the morning shift at all four shops.
----------------------
Oakmere Bakery
Order reference: CK-3187
March 12
Dear Mr. Yates,
Thank you for your order for a medium cake for the weekend of March 28.
You placed that order at our Priory Street shop, which is having its ovens repaired during the last week of March. No baking will be done there that week.
Every medium cake for that weekend has already been promised to other customers, so we will bake you a large cake instead. You will still pay only the price of the medium size.
Your cake will be ready at the shop that bakes large cakes and opens at eight o'clock on weekends. Please pick it up before noon, as any cake left at closing time is sold in the shop.
Monica Ibarra
Orders Manager
Order changes can be made only at our Eastcote shop, where our order records are kept.

Monica Ibarra

A Family Kitchen Opens Its Doors for a Monthly Dinner
By Regina Toft
Nora Halverson, who runs the kitchen at her family's restaurant on Colton Road, has just launched a monthly evening for a handful of paying guests. Apart from this event, the restaurant continues to serve its full menu of simple home-style meals to local residents.
"Each month we set out one fixed menu of four courses," she says. "Guests sit around the counter to watch me cook every dish and listen while I explain what goes into it." The idea came from her regular customers. Some have eaten there since her parents opened the restaurant thirty-two years ago, and many kept asking to see how their favorite dishes were made.
Only ten seats are available each month, and places must be reserved ahead by telephoning the restaurant directly. A payment of forty dollars is taken at the time of booking, and the next evening will be held on the first Friday of April.

Advance Holding of Bicycle Spaces on Scheduled Buses
Issued by the Passenger Office, Kilbourne Bus Lines
In force from February 9
Last season, requests to carry bicycles on our daytime services were more numerous than the spaces then provided on board. Each bus on our daytime network has since been fitted with four bicycle spaces, and these may be held before travel.
1. Ask for a space at any staffed ticket counter at least 24 hours before departure. Requests made after that time cannot be accepted, even when a space is empty.
2. Pick up your printed confirmation at the same counter before boarding.

April 17
Subject: Request TR-2864, transfer between class sections
Dear Mr. Ferreira,

Sincerely,
Judith Vance
Enrollment Officer

Terrace Dining at The Sycamore Table
The terrace beside the main entrance is back in service for the warm season, from the first week of May until the end of September. During that time, food is served outdoors from 11:30 A.M. to 9:00 P.M. on every day the restaurant is open. The terrace tables stand under the trees and are screened from the street, and lap blankets are brought out on request when evenings turn cool. --[1]--.
What Is Served Outdoors
Terrace orders come from the same kitchen as the dining room, and the outdoor menu is drawn from the dining room menu rather than repeating it in full. Any item on it can also be packed to take home. Dishes are cooked to order, so a short wait is normal at busy times. --[2]--.
Finding a Seat
Terrace tables are not reserved. Reservations are taken only for the dining room indoors. --[3]--. Guests give their name to the host and are seated in order of arrival. Sixteen more seats will be added to the terrace once new planters and screens are installed, which is expected in late July. Each terrace table seats up to six guests. Groups of seven or more are asked to reserve a table in the dining room. --[4]--. Such groups are therefore encouraged to book several days ahead.
The Sycamore Table welcomes terrace guests throughout the season.

Business Services
Yardley Office Support Ends Charges for Repair Visits
By Theodore Sinclair
March 25
Yardley Office Support is replacing the fee it has charged office clients for each repair visit. Until now, the company has sent an invoice every time a technician was sent out. Under the new arrangement, clients instead register their individual machines with the company, and the number of machines a client registers decides how quickly the company responds when a problem is reported.
According to Vernon Middleton, the aim is to match the speed of service to how much a client depends on the company. "We wanted a simple and fair basis, one that ties our attention to how much equipment a client relies on us to look after," he said. Under the new terms, a client that registers five or more machines is promised same-day response, while a client with fewer than five is given next-day response.
Existing customers will be brought onto the new arrangement in stages over the next three months. Offices holding the largest service agreements will be switched over first, followed by the smaller ones, so that the company can confirm each client's registered machines before the old charges are removed from the account.
[A sample coverage record issued to one client office is printed alongside this report.]

Yardley Office Support is replacing the fee it has charged office clients for each repair visit. Until now, the company has sent an invoice every time a technician was sent out. Existing customers will be brought onto the new arrangement in stages over the next three months. Evening League Adds a Third Division
Twenty-two teams entered the evening league at Riverbend Sports Center last spring, playing in just two divisions. Organizers say that arrangement put teams of very different sizes against one another, and several matches were settled long before the final minutes.
"A squad of ten was facing a squad of twenty, and neither side enjoyed it," said Beatrice Kowalski, the center's recreation programs manager.
Entries are therefore sorted this season by the number of players registered, with the largest squads placed in Division One and the smallest in Division Three. Division One plays on Tuesday evenings and the newly added Division Two on Wednesday evenings, while Division Three plays on Thursday evenings. Monday evenings are kept free for rescheduled games.
Entry forms are available at the front desk.
Clive Bannister, Community Affairs

Brindley Self Storage rents units to residential and commercial customers on flexible month-to-month terms, and every rental includes insurance for stored belongings and 24-hour gated access. Units range from a single walk-in locker to a space the size of a large garage. Prices rise with the size of the unit, and new customers pay only for the days left in their first month.
Visit any of our branches, where a site coordinator will help you choose a unit. Warren Bledsoe runs our Kirkby site, and Priya Naidu looks after Alderton. Geoffrey Talbot manages Roxton, while Lorraine Ackerman leads the team at Farndon.
Reserve online at www.brindleystorage.com or call 555-0173. Front desks are open daily from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m.
----------------------
Rating: 4 out of 5
Verified renter — Bethany Corliss, July 8
I signed up with Brindley after my spare room filled up with boxes. Reserving a unit through the website was simple. When I arrived, the site coordinator, Lorraine Ackerman, had my paperwork ready and walked me straight to my locker. My one regret is the size I settled on. questions.passage:
Community News
Trentham Library to Close for Roof Repairs
By Jonas Eckhart, The Vale Chronicle
The town's busiest library branch, Trentham, will close on Tuesday, March 1, and is expected to remain closed until early June.
Although the repairs were originally scheduled for next year, it was the discovery of water damage above the reading room that caused them to be advanced. The town council has also increased the funds set aside for the project, and the additional money will pay for a renovated reading room that, once the branch reopens, will accommodate more readers than the one at Rushden, currently the largest in town.
In the meantime, each of Trentham's services has been relocated to another branch. The branches taking them over include Wadebridge, the town's oldest library, and Blaxton, its newest, which opened only last year.
"For our members, it will be business as usual, just at a different address," said Deborah Guthrie, the town's head librarian. The Library Services Office has published a full list of the temporary arrangements.
----------------------
Library Services Office
Where to go while the Trentham branch is closed
Service	Moves to	Please note
Borrowing and returns	Rushden branch	Open every day. Bring your library card.
Children's story hour	Wadebridge branch	Saturday mornings. No booking needed.
Evening reading group	Rushden branch	Monday evenings only. Sign up at the desk.
Computer help desk*	Blaxton branch	Thursday afternoons only. Please arrive early.
* Each help desk visit lasts twenty minutes. Sign in when you arrive.
Please do not wait until Trentham closes on Tuesday, March 1, to return or renew items borrowed there.
Questions about any service may go to staff at any open branch.
----------------------
Northside Community Newsletter
Library Events This Week
Although the Trentham branch remains closed for repairs, two of its regular activities continue elsewhere this week.
Monday evening: the reading group will discuss a travel book, with Felix Kovacs leading the conversation.
Saturday morning: the children's story hour, read as usual by Iris Okafor, who has led it for six years.
The next listing of community events will appear in Sunday's edition.

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
WAVERLY, October 6
Crowhurst Vehicle Rental to Accept Returns at Any Branch
Cars and small vans may be left at a branch other than the one that supplied them.
Crowhurst Vehicle Rental announced today that from November 2 a car or small van rented at one of its branches may be left at any other Crowhurst branch. Until now, every vehicle had to be brought back to the branch that supplied it.
Customers are asked to tell the receiving branch at least twenty-four hours before arrival so that a space can be held for the vehicle. The change does not cover the company's delivery trucks, which are rented under a separate weekly agreement. In addition, business customers whose account agreement names a single return branch must ask for that agreement to be amended before their next rental.
"Drivers have been asking us for this for years, and we are glad to make it standard," said Yusuf Adeyemi, director of customer service. "Daily rates stay exactly as they are."
The new option should be especially useful because of the size of the company's network. Five years ago Crowhurst was operating from thirty-eight sites. It now serves drivers from sixty-two, the newest of which opened in August.
Crowhurst Vehicle Rental supplies cars, small vans and delivery trucks to private and business customers across the country.
General questions: Heather Osborne, Customer Information Manager, h.osborne@crowhurstrental.com
Business accounts: Miguel Fontaine, Business Accounts Manager, m.fontaine@crowhurstrental.com

Curtis Holloway
Personal Banking Manager

Transportation
Airport Splits Its Parking Into Three Areas
The single lot at Linden Regional Airport has become three areas with separate rules and rates.
By Nolan Sedgwick, Transportation Reporter
Since June, drivers at Linden Regional Airport have parked in one of three areas instead of the single lot that served the terminal for years. Over the first two months, staff counted about a third more vehicles left overnight than in the same period last year, and most of that increase was recorded in Elmgate.
The three areas differ in how they charge. Drivers who leave a car for only a few hours can pay by the hour in Elmgate, while those who stay longer are charged by the day or, in Tilbury, by the week.
"Offering drivers a choice of distance and price has filled spaces that used to sit empty," said Yvonne Salcedo, who manages airport operations. "I accept that many regular travelers who once walked to the terminal from their cars now ride the shuttle instead, and not all of them are pleased."
A further change takes effect on October 1, when Cransley will begin holding its spaces for drivers with reservations and will no longer allow any stay to run beyond four days. Drivers who plan longer stays, or who arrive without a booking, will need to use one of the other two areas.
A full comparison of the three areas appears below.
----------------------
Passenger Parking: Comparison of Areas
Rules in force since June 1
Covers the three passenger areas only. Staff and rental vehicles use a separate area that is closed to passengers.
Cransley	Elmgate	Tilbury
Access to terminal	On foot	Free shuttle bus	Free shuttle bus
Time to terminal	6 minutes	12 minutes	18 minutes
Maximum stay	30 days until October 1, then 4 days	30 days	60 days
Charges	Per day	Per hour for the first 3 hours, then per day	Per week (b)
Advance booking	Required from October 1 (a)	Not required	Not required
Vehicle height limit	None	2.1 meters	None
(a) Cransley reservations close at 6:00 P.M. on the day before arrival.
(b) In Tilbury, each period of seven days is charged as one week, and a partial week is charged as a full week.
Reserve online at lindenairport.com/parking.

Transportation
Airport Splits Its Parking Into Three Areas
The single lot at Linden Regional Airport has become three areas with separate rules and rates.
By Nolan Sedgwick, Transportation Reporter
Since June, drivers at Linden Regional Airport have parked in one of three areas instead of the single lot that served the terminal for years. Over the first two months, staff counted about a third more vehicles left overnight than in the same period last year, and most of that increase was recorded in Elmgate.
The three areas differ in how they charge. Drivers who leave a car for only a few hours can pay by the hour in Elmgate, while those who stay longer are charged by the day or, in Tilbury, by the week.
"Offering drivers a choice of distance and price has filled spaces that used to sit empty," said Yvonne Salcedo, who manages airport operations. "I accept that many regular travelers who once walked to the terminal from their cars now ride the shuttle instead, and not all of them are pleased."
A further change takes effect on October 1, when Cransley will begin holding its spaces for drivers with reservations and will no longer allow any stay to run beyond four days. Drivers who plan longer stays, or who arrive without a booking, will need to use one of the other two areas.
A full comparison of the three areas appears below.
----------------------

Rules in force since June 1
Covers the three passenger areas only. Staff and rental vehicles use a separate area that is closed to passengers.
Cransley	Elmgate	Tilbury
Access to terminal	On foot	Free shuttle bus	Free shuttle bus

Maximum stay	30 days until October 1, then 4 days	30 days	60 days

(a) Cransley reservations close at 6:00 P.M. on the day before arrival.

Local News
Careers evening moves to a larger home
Organizers expect the largest turnout so far
By Hugh Pettigrew
The Milford Careers Partnership will hold its careers and training open evening at Selby Conference Center on Thursday, November 13. The evening has been offered every autumn since 2018, but growing attendance has moved it out of the community hall used in earlier years.
Until last year, visitors simply joined a line for whichever session they wanted. This time the sessions, still twenty minutes long as in past years, are allotted in advance, and only visitors holding a confirmation record will be seated. "We were turning people away at eight o'clock, which nobody enjoyed," said Constance Mabry, who has coordinated the evening from the beginning.
Sessions are offered on writing an application at 6:15, interview practice at 6:45, choosing a training course at 7:30, and starting a small business at 8:15. A briefing on hiring support at 7:00 is open only to visitors registered in the employer category.
Visitors registered as students must bring a document showing that they are enrolled in a course. Employers are asked to bring printed details of the positions they hope to fill. Places can be reserved at milfordcareers.org by November 10, and admission is free.
----------------------

Telephone: 555-0165

Business Notes
Lunch Deliveries Move to Fixed Routes
By Douglas Pascoe, Business Reporter
Until now, clients of Mowbray Office Catering could ask for delivery on any weekday, so orders from one street often traveled on three vans. "The food was never the problem," said operations director Hannah Villanueva. "We were sending drivers through the same districts twice before noon."
To address this, from April 6 each service area will have a regular route with a single delivery day, prepared at one of the company's two kitchens. Under the new schedule, the Ellerby Street kitchen will start an hour early on Thursdays, since that day's route will carry more meals than any other.
Route details appear in the delivery schedule.
----------------------
Mowbray Office Catering — Lunch Delivery Routes
In effect from April 6
Route	Service areas	Kitchen	Delivery day	Order cutoff	Minimum order
L1	Duxford, Sowerby	Ellerby	Tuesday	3 P.M., two working days ahead	12 meals
L2	Grenford	Ellerby	Thursday	3 P.M., two working days ahead	12 meals
L3	Tenbury, Eddington	Hadleigh	Friday	Noon, three working days ahead	15 meals
L4	All areas, on request	Hadleigh	Wednesday	Noon, three working days ahead	25 meals
Route L3 orders cannot be increased after the cutoff.
Queries about routes L1 and L2 go to Owen Duarte. Queries about routes L3 and L4 go to Lucia Chowdhury.
----------------------
To: Miriam Vogel, Ockford Design Partners
Subject: Change to your lunch deliveries
Account: LD-6193
From: Karl Jessup
Date: March 18
Dear Ms. Vogel,
From April 6, our lunch deliveries will run on fixed routes. Your office has taken our Wednesday delivery for six years. However, your area, Duxford, has now been assigned to route L1, which delivers on Tuesdays.
You may either accept Tuesday delivery or keep your Wednesday delivery by ordering through route L4. Each route's cutoff and minimum order appear in the published schedule.
Please reply by April 1 naming the arrangement you prefer. The coordinator responsible for Duxford's assigned route will then call you to confirm your choice.
Karl Jessup
Order Desk Manager
Order desk hours: Tuesday through Friday, 8 A.M. to 4 P.M. Replies reach the shared desk, not the sender.

Office Machine Repairs at Halverton
By Trevor Nilsen, Services Correspondent
Halverton Equipment Care, which services office beverage machines across the district, now handles reported faults in one of two ways. A technician visits the client's own office, or the machine is collected and repaired at the company's service center. Either option is offered within one week.
Rachel Tomlin, the firm's service manager, said the second option was added last year because requests for same-week visits were rising faster than technicians could keep up with. "Now every client can be given a fixed date for the work," she said.
Both options are available under the standard care agreement, which includes servicing of up to six machines at each client address. Replaceable supplies such as water filters are billed separately.
Full terms appear in the company's printed price list.
----------------------
To: Service Department, Halverton Equipment Care
From: Teresa Kilbride, Marnfield Insurance Services
Date: September 22
Subject: Kitchen machine fault
Reference: Care agreement MC-2740
Dear Service Department,
Your team handled our last fault promptly, and we were pleased. Now the machine in our ground-floor kitchen has stopped heating water, and we would like to arrange a repair.
Our first choice is a technician visit here within the next three days. If no technician is free this week, please collect the machine and repair it at your service center. Your terms state that a machine is lent to us at no charge while ours is away. Could you confirm today which arrangement you will make?
For your records, we also installed two more machines in the upstairs kitchen last month, so eight are now in use at this address.
Sincerely,
Teresa Kilbride
Office Manager
Direct extension 176
----------------------
Halverton Equipment Care
Bill to: Marnfield Insurance Services
Document number: 7156
Issue date: September 30
Agreement reference: MC-2740
Service date: September 24
Off-site servicing, one unit — included under agreement — $0.00
Replacement water filter*, one unit — $34.00
Total due — $34.00
*Replaceable supplies are not included in the standard care agreement.
Payment is due within 14 days. Please include the document number above with your payment so that it can be matched to your account. Questions about charges should go to the service department, not to this billing office.
